===== TICKET =====
KS-1467 — AppError resets every subclass to the base prototype: `instanceof <subclass>` is always false and ValidationError `details` (password-strength feedback) never reaches the client [In Progress]

## BLUF

`AppError`'s constructor ends with `Object.setPrototypeOf(this, AppError.prototype)`, which resets every subclass instance to the **base** prototype. So `err instanceof ValidationError` (or any other subclass) is **always false**, and `errorHandler` never adds `details` to a 422. The password-strength `feedback` that registration, password reset and password change build is silently dropped. The same constructor line is in `packages/shared`, which twelve other services mount.

## Recommendation

Make the constructor `Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype)` in both places, with a cell per subclass, and decide deliberately that 422 responses now carry `details` (a visible response change; check the published 422 shape first). Until then, code that needs to recognise an error by type must use `statusCode`/`code`, as the tests do.

## Detail

* **Measured 2026-10-12** by driving the real `errorHandler` in `services/auth`: `next(new ValidationError('New password is too weak', { feedback: ['add a number'] }))` answers 422 with the body `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"New password is too weak"}}`. No `details`. And `new ValidationError('x', { a: 1 }) instanceof ValidationError` is `false`.
* **The dead branch:** `services/auth/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts:296`, `if (err instanceof ValidationError && err.details) { errorPayload.details = err.details; }`. The outer `err instanceof AppError` works (the base), the inner one cannot.
* **What is dropped today** (`new ValidationError(..., { feedback })`): `routes/auth.ts:201` (register) and `:819` (reset-password), `routes/users.ts:981` (change-password). I have not checked the other services' use.
* **Where the constructor line is:** `services/auth/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts:25` and `packages/shared/src/errors/index.ts:44`. Whether the shared handler has the same `details` branch is unmeasured.
* **How it bit me:** a new `err instanceof ServiceUnavailableError` check in the KS-1188 F3 change never matched. It was caught only because the new test went red against the fix; the fix keys on `statusCode === 503`.
* **Not established:** whether any client depends on `details` being absent; whether any other `instanceof <subclass>` exists outside `services/auth` (the one grep covered `Blockchain/Dev/services` and found only the two above).

Found by Seat V 3rd while building KS-1188 F3, 2026-10-12. Related: KS-1188, KS-253 (the 503 class).

## Gate notes carried from #1479 (KS-1188 F3, same file family; Sonnet-tier gate, verdict sha256/16 `306acc1aaf41a045`)

1. `services/auth/src/services/passwordLoginGate.ts`: a `const` (BACKUP_CODE_UNCONFIRMED_MESSAGE) and its import sit in the middle of the import block, before `import { STATUSES_MAY_RECEIVE_CREDENTIAL }`. Cosmetic; lint passes. Move it below the imports.
2. `ks1188-f3-a-spent-backup-code-503-says-so.test.ts`: no cell asserts the burn runs exactly once (the gate verified it by a probe only: UPDATE count 1 in the faulted case). Add one.

+// KS-1467 (packages/shared src/errors/index.ts, mounted by twelve services): AppError's constructor ended with `Object.setPrototypeOf(this, AppError.prototype)`, which resets EVERY subclass
+// instance to the base prototype, so `err instanceof <subclass>` was always false. The constructor now uses `new.target.prototype`. P1/P2/P3 pin the prototypes (three levels deep for
+// DocumentNotFoundError); C1/C2 pin what must not change: the status, the code, the details, and the handler's answer.
+import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
+import type { Response } from 'express';
+import {
+  errorHandler,
+  AppError,
+  BadRequestError,
+  UnauthorizedError,
+  ForbiddenError,
+  NotFoundError,
+  ConflictError,
+  ValidationError,
+  RateLimitError,
+  InternalError,
+  ServiceUnavailableError,
+  DocumentNotFoundError,
+} from '../errors';
+
+const FACTORIES = [
+  { name: 'BadRequestError', make: () => new BadRequestError('x'), cls: BadRequestError, status: 400 },
+  { name: 'UnauthorizedError', make: () => new UnauthorizedError('x'), cls: UnauthorizedError, status: 401 },
+  { name: 'ForbiddenError', make: () => new ForbiddenError('x'), cls: ForbiddenError, status: 403 },
+  { name: 'NotFoundError', make: () => new NotFoundError('Thing'), cls: NotFoundError, status: 404 },
+  { name: 'ConflictError', make: () => new ConflictError('x'), cls: ConflictError, status: 409 },
+  { name: 'ValidationError', make: () => new ValidationError('x', { a: 1 }), cls: ValidationError, status: 422 },
+  { name: 'RateLimitError', make: () => new RateLimitError(5), cls: RateLimitError, status: 429 },
+  { name: 'InternalError', make: () => new InternalError('x'), cls: InternalError, status: 500 },
+  { name: 'ServiceUnavailableError', make: () => new ServiceUnavailableError('Billing'), cls: ServiceUnavailableError, status: 503 },
+] as const;
+
+function run(err: Error): { statusCode: number; body: { error: { code: string; message: string; details?: unknown } } } {
+  const captured = { statusCode: 0, body: undefined } as unknown as { statusCode: number; body: { error: { code: string; message: string; details?: unknown } } };
+  const res = {
+    status(code: number) {
+      captured.statusCode = code;
+      return this;
+    },
+    json(payload: unknown) {
+      captured.body = payload as typeof captured.body;
+      return this;
+    },
+  } as unknown as Response;
+  errorHandler(err, undefined, res, undefined);
+  return captured;
+}
+
+describe('KS-1467: shared AppError subclasses keep their own prototype', () => {
+  it.each(FACTORIES)('RED KS-1467 P1 $name: an instance is an instance of its own class', ({ make, cls }) => {
+    expect(make() instanceof cls).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it.each(FACTORIES)('RED KS-1467 P2 $name: the prototype of an instance is the class prototype', ({ make, cls }) => {
+    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(make())).toBe(cls.prototype);
+  });
+
+  it('RED KS-1467 P3 a two-level subclass is an instance of every class in its chain', () => {
+    const e = new DocumentNotFoundError('d-1');
+    expect([e instanceof DocumentNotFoundError, e instanceof NotFoundError, e instanceof AppError]).toEqual([true, true, true]);
+  });
+
+  it.each(FACTORIES)('control KS-1467 C1 $name: an instance is still an AppError and an Error with its status', ({ make, status }) => {
+    const e = make();
+    expect([e instanceof AppError, e instanceof Error, e.statusCode]).toEqual([true, true, status]);
+  });
+
+  it('control KS-1467 C2 the handler still answers a ValidationError with its details and a 422', () => {
+    const r = run(new ValidationError('bad', { field: 'name' }));
+    expect(r.statusCode).toBe(422);
+    expect(r.body.error).toEqual({ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: 'bad', details: { field: 'name' } });
+  });
+});

97: export class ValidationError extends AppError {
98:   constructor(message: string = 'Validation failed', details?: unknown) {
99:     super(message, 422, 'VALIDATION_ERROR', true, details);
100:   }
101: }
102: 
103: /**
104:  * 429 Too Many Requests
105:  */
106: export class RateLimitError extends AppError {
107:   constructor(retryAfter?: number) {
108:     super('Too many requests', 429, 'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED', true, { retryAfter });
109:   }
110: }
111: 
112: /**
113:  * 500 Internal Server Error
114:  */
115: export class InternalError extends AppError {
116:   constructor(message: string = 'Internal server error') {
117:     super(message, 500, 'INTERNAL_ERROR', false);
118:   }
119: }

123:  */

125:   constructor(service: string = 'Service') {
126:     super(`${service} is temporarily unavailable`, 503, 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', true);
127:   }

195:   constructor(message: string, details?: unknown) {

197:   }
198: }
199: 
200: // =============================================================================
201: // ERROR RESPONSE FORMATTER
202: // =============================================================================
203: 
204: export interface ErrorResponse {
205:   success: false;
206:   error: {
207:     code: string;
208:     message: string;
209:     details?: unknown;
210:   };
211:   requestId?: string;
212: }
213: 
214: export function formatErrorResponse(error: AppError, requestId?: string): ErrorResponse {
215:   return {
216:     success: false,
217:     error: {
218:       code: error.code,
219:       message: error.message,
220:       details: error.details,
221:     },
222:     requestId,
223:   };
224: }
225: 
226: // =============================================================================
227: // ERROR HANDLER MIDDLEWARE
228: // =============================================================================
229: 
230: export function errorHandler(
231:   err: Error,
232:   _req: unknown,
233:   res: Response,
234:   _next: unknown
235: ): void {
236:   // Log the error
237:   logger.error('Error occurred', {
238:     error: err.message,
239:     stack: err.stack,
240:     ...(err instanceof AppError && { code: err.code, statusCode: err.statusCode }),
241:   });
242: 
243:   // Handle Zod validation errors
244:   if (err instanceof ZodError) {
245:     const validationError = new ValidationError('Validation failed', err.errors);
246:     res.status(validationError.statusCode).json(formatErrorResponse(validationError));
247:     return;
248:   }
249: 
250:   // Handle AppError
251:   if (err instanceof AppError) {
252:     res.status(err.statusCode).json(formatErrorResponse(err));
253:     return;
254:   }
255: 
256:   // Handle body-parser errors (malformed JSON, oversized / unsupported body).
257:   // These arrive as a SyntaxError / typed error carrying `.type` + `.status`
258:   // but are NOT AppError, so they'd otherwise fall through to the 500 below —
259:   // flattening a client's bad request into a server error. A malformed body is
260:   // a client error (KS-144 / KS-111: stop turning bad input into 500).
261:   const bp = err as Error & { type?: string; status?: number };
262:   if (bp.type === 'entity.parse.failed' || (err instanceof SyntaxError && 'body' in (err as object))) {
263:     const badRequest = new BadRequestError('Malformed request body');
264:     res.status(badRequest.statusCode).json(formatErrorResponse(badRequest));
265:     return;
266:   }
267:   if (typeof bp.status === 'number' && bp.status >= 400 && bp.status < 500) {
268:     const clientErr = new AppError(err.message || 'Bad request', bp.status, 'BAD_REQUEST', true);
269:     res.status(clientErr.statusCode).json(formatErrorResponse(clientErr));
270:     return;
271:   }
272: 
273:   // Handle unknown errors.
274:   //
275:   // KS-727: the message is generic on EVERY environment, not only production.
276:   // The old gate was `NODE_ENV === 'production' ? <generic> : err.message`, so
277:   // anything that was not the exact string `production` — `development`,
278:   // `demo`, `test`, or unset — returned the thrown message verbatim to the
279:   // caller. KS-658 records that the live demo runs all 26 Node services as
280:   // `NODE_ENV=development`, so on the demo that was the branch that always
281:   // executed, and it leaked driver text (`invalid byte sequence for encoding
282:   // "UTF8": 0x00`) and internal call sites (`role.split is not a function`)
283:   // from ordinary requests.
284:   //
285:   // Nothing is lost: `err.message` and `err.stack` are already logged at the
286:   // top of this handler, so the detail still reaches the operator — it just
287:   // stops reaching the caller. Typed client errors are unaffected; they return
288:   // above, carrying their own authored text.
289:   const internalError = new InternalError('An unexpected error occurred');
290:   res.status(internalError.statusCode).json(formatErrorResponse(internalError));
291: }
292: 
293: // =============================================================================
294: // ASYNC HANDLER WRAPPER
295: // =============================================================================
296: 
297: type AsyncFunction = (req: unknown, res: Response, next: (err?: unknown) => void) => Promise<unknown>;
298: 
299: export function asyncHandler(fn: AsyncFunction) {
300:   return (req: unknown, res: Response, next: (err?: unknown) => void) => {
301:     Promise.resolve(fn(req, res, next)).catch(next);
302:   };
303: }

409: <h1>🔐 API Security/Functional Testing Architecture &amp; Flow Diagrams</h1>
410: <!-- ===== COLOUR KEY ===== -->
411: <div class="ckey">
412: <h3>
413:         🛡️ Post-run gates — judging the RUN, not its assertions (KS-517 ·
414:         KS-684)
415:       </h3>
416: <div class="ck-note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
417:         Gates run <em>after</em> a Schemathesis sweep and feed the exit
418:         code alongside the check results (run validity, NDJSON completeness,
419:         report reconciliation, triaged baseline, plus the authenticated-coverage
420:         gate). </td><td>They exist because every
421:         assertion-based gate shares one blind spot:
422:         <strong>a check that never ran cannot fail</strong>, so a run that
423:         tested nothing scores clean everywhere. Each of these answers “did
424:         this run have the standing to say anything?” rather than
425:         “what did it say?”
426:       </td></tr></table></div>
427: <div class="ck-group">
428:         The gates — and how the sweep’s own exit code is read
429:         (KS-1408)
430:       </div>
431: <table class="ck-matrix"><thead><tr><th>Status</th><th>Gate / check</th><th>What it does</th></tr></thead><tbody>
432: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Authenticated coverage (KS-517)</strong></td><td>a sweep that loses its session still calls every operation, but the requests die at the auth middleware and never reach a handler. Measured from <code>schemathesis-metrics.jsonl</code>. Caught 240/309 operations stuck at 401.</td></tr>
433: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Run validity (KS-684)</strong></td><td>declares a run <strong>INVALID</strong> when errors dominate: more than <strong>10%</strong> of operations erroring, <em>or</em> <strong>5+</strong> operations sharing one identical error message. Read from the run’s own JUnit XML, deliberately not from the report’s parsers, so the gate can disagree with the report. Reconstructed against the 2026-08-24 incident (310 of 318 operations = 97.5%) → INVALID.</td></tr>
434: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Report reconciliation (KS-517)</strong></td><td>the HTML report’s headline numbers must equal Schemathesis’ own console summary. Enforces the three-way parity MUST: <code>console = results.json = HTML report</code>. Fails closed — a missing artefact is “cannot verify”, never a pass. <!-- KS-1408: the caveat below was missing; the gate's reachability is KS-752 --> <strong>Caveat:</strong> <code>run.py</code> evaluates it (and the baseline gate) only when every earlier gate passed, so it is skipped on any sweep that found failures — open as KS-752. Until that lands, run it by hand on such a run.</td></tr>
435: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Sweep outcome (KS-1408)</strong></td><td>Schemathesis 4.29.0 made exit <strong>2</strong> mean “nothing tested, or a schema / config / internal error” and <strong>130</strong> mean “interrupted”. <code>src/sweep_outcome.py</code> classifies the exit code once — PASSED (0), FAILED (1), INVALID (2), TIMED OUT (124, the harness’s own kill), INTERRUPTED (130), UNKNOWN (anything else) — and the console <code>Status:</code> line, <code>results.json</code> and the Verdict section’s <strong>Outcome</strong> row all render that one value. Previously every non-zero code was recorded as <code>failed</code>, and at 4.28.0 a sweep that tested nothing exited 0. Only PASSED is green.</td></tr>
436: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Closing banner (KS-571)</strong></td><td>the banner at the end of a run now counts <em>every</em> gate that feeds the exit code (run validity, NDJSON completeness, report reconciliation, triaged baseline, IDOR, integration, anchoring, preconditions, auth coverage) and names a gated suite that was <strong>skipped</strong>, with its reason, instead of printing OVERALL: PASSED over a failing exit code. This reverses KS-684's narrower banner (sweep and IDOR only).</td></tr>
437: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Known tool false-positive class, kept visible (KS-1414)</strong></td><td>from Schemathesis 4.29.x a negative case can have its mutated body overwritten by a pool-drawn valid value, so the platform rightly accepts a VALID request and <code>negative_data_rejection</code> still reports “Invalid data should have been rejected” (55–95 per full sweep). A report section, a console block and a <code>results.json</code> block count them; nothing is filtered or baselined, and it is informational, not a gate. Since 2026-10-07 the same rule covers <code>by_design_input_tolerance_guard</code>: a request valid as sent (a drawn-over body, or a path whose values are each drawn or valid) no longer fails the guard, and the section counts the guard’s failures and its valid-as-sent passes. Of the guard’s 12 failures on the KS-1439 sweeps, 6 were valid as sent and 6 genuine (<code>audit-log</code> <code>limit=201</code>, KS-1359).</td></tr>
438: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>One run is one draw — seed + <code>--repeat N</code> (KS-1680)</strong></td><td>a failure appears only when the run's random seed draws the case that reaches it, and sometimes only when another operation in the same sweep created its data: three <code>pr</code> runs on one build found <strong>11 / 9 / 8</strong> failures. Every run now states its seed <em>and whether it was fixed</em> on the console, in <code>results.json</code> and in the Overview. <code>run.py &lt;tier&gt; --repeat N</code> runs the tier N times (each a complete normal run) and counts each pair as <strong>k/N</strong> — N/N deterministic, k/N seed-dependent — then sweeps every failing operation <em>alone</em> on the same seeds: a pair that never fails alone is flagged <em>needs other operations' data</em>; an isolated sweep that tested nothing is <em>inconclusive</em>, never a pass. The baseline gate over a set fails an untriaged pair seen in <em>any</em> run, and <code>--compare</code> calls a pair fixed only at N/N → 0/N on a check that inspects the response <em>and</em> when the later set reached the status it failed on (otherwise <em>not reached</em>; a check that fails on its status reads <em>gone (not proven fixed)</em>). The single-run Delta tab now compares only with an earlier run of the <em>same profile</em> (a first pre-merge was once diffed against a pr run: 69 bogus “regressions”).</td></tr>
439: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Fresh-clone preconditions (KS-955)</strong></td><td>a fresh clone used to fail every suite at login in a way that read as a product regression: unseeded personas 401'd (a 100% k6 error rate, an INVALID sweep), the failed logins tripped the F-06 lockout, and with no <code>GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET</code> the cross-tenant tests reported “BUG-ISOLATION-001 regression” (KS-1704). Each suite now logs its personas in <strong>once</strong> before it sends anything — Schemathesis <code>run.py</code>, Akto's <code>personaLoginSetup</code>, k6's runner, Playwright's <code>auth-setup</code> — and stops with <code>KS-955 precondition:</code> and the causes in order (not seeded, locked out, wrong password). The two cross-tenant tests use <code>gateway_vouch_active</code>: it sets a random per-run vouch secret on a local stack the user owns and restores it, or fails with the precondition, never the regression wording. <code>bootstrap-env.sh</code> now generates the secret for a fresh clone, and the lockout reset is in <code>systemTest/CLAUDE.md</code>.</td></tr>
440: </tbody></table>
441: <div class="ck-group">
442:         The same blind spot in Akto — a template that was selected but never ran
443:         (KS-710 · KS-717)
444:       </div>
445: <div class="ck-note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
446:         Akto’s version of “a check that never ran cannot
447:         fail”. </td><td>The test-id catalog is generated from the template
448:         <strong>files</strong>, and <code>check-test-ids</code> diffs that
449:         render against the committed catalog — both sides file-derived, so it is
450:         <em>structurally incapable</em> of noticing that Akto never loaded a
451:         template. A selected-but-absent id produces no
452:         <code>testing_run_result</code> document at all, and Akto reports
453:         <code>vulnerable 0</code> exactly as it does for a template that ran and
454:         found nothing. Measured on the full OWASP run, 2026-08-28, Akto 2.22.2:
455:         <strong>207 ids selected, 193 exercised, verdict PASS</strong>.
456:         Re-measured on slot 2, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6 (KS-1286):
457:         <strong>194 templates initiated, 50,018 result docs across 347
458:           endpoints</strong>
459:         — the regenerated catalog is byte-identical to 2.22.2’s, and
460:         207→194 is KS-717 dropping ids Akto could never execute rather than
461:         lost coverage.
462:       </td></tr></table></div>
463: <table class="ck-matrix"><thead><tr><th>Status</th><th>Gate / check</th><th>What it does</th></tr></thead><tbody>
464: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Catalog vs loaded library (KS-717)</strong></td><td>a live assertion in <code>SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1 npm run test:setup</code> reads <code>yaml_templates</code> straight from Mongo (<code>src/setup/loadedTemplates.ts</code>, slot-aware via <code>AKTO_PREFIX</code>) and diffs it against the catalog <strong>in both directions</strong>, failing on drift either way. Accepted differences are ticketed entries in <code>KNOWN_CATALOG_DRIFT</code>, and the test also fails when a listed entry <em>stops</em> drifting — an exemption cannot outlive its reason.</td></tr>
465: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Excluded from the catalog</strong></td><td>an id Akto can never execute must not be selected. 8 Threat-Protection rules carry no <code>execute:</code> block (KS-710); 5 carry upstream’s <code>inactive: true</code>, which Akto stores but its engine skips via <code>fetchOnlyActive</code> (KS-717 §3). 1 more (<code>BYPASS_CAPTCHA_REMOVING_COOKIE</code>) Akto refuses to store, because its <code>info.references:</code> is empty and Jackson cannot coerce that to a list. Catalog <strong>207 → 199 → 194 ids</strong>.</td></tr>
466: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong>Reported, never silent</strong></td><td><code>load-templates</code> names every file Akto rejected and Akto’s own <code>actionErrors</code>; <code>generate-test-ids</code> reports exclusions and, separately, files with a YAML defect Akto tolerates and we now tolerate too (which ARE catalogued — <code>LFI_IN_HEADERS_LINUX</code> had never executed once). The HTML report renders <strong>exercised / selected</strong> with the shortfall named, not a bare count.</td></tr>
467: </tbody></table>
468: <div class="ck-group">
469:         Outcome taxonomy — five categories, shared across all three surfaces
470:       </div>
471: <div class="ck-note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
472:         The taxonomy is <strong>closed and shared</strong>: a category exists in
473:         the console, in <code>results.json</code> and in the HTML report, with
474:         the same label and the same count, or it is a design error.
475:         <code>results.json</code> is the source of truth; the other two are
476:         renderings of it. Each run also writes Schemathesis's native HTML report at <code>&lt;run&gt;/schemathesis-native-html/index.html</code> (linked from the harness report; KS-1615).
477:       </td></tr></table></div>
478: <div class="ck-row">
479: <div class="ck-item">
480: <span class="ck-sw ck-success"></span> <strong>PASS</strong> —
481:           exercised, no violation
482:         </div>
483: <div class="ck-item">
484: <span class="ck-sw ck-fail"></span> <strong>FAIL</strong> — exercised,
485:           violated a check
486:         </div>
487: <div class="ck-item">
488: <span class="ck-sw ck-notwired"></span> <strong>UNVERIFIED</strong> —
489:           should have run, did not; gates the run (KS-478)
490:         </div>
491: <div class="ck-item">
492: <span class="ck-sw ck-infra"></span> <strong>OUT OF SCOPE</strong> —
493:           excluded by mode, not by accident (KS-519)
494:         </div>
495: <div class="ck-item">
496: <span class="ck-sw ck-tool"></span> <strong>SKIPPED</strong> — a
497:           precondition was never met (KS-684)
498:         </div>
499: </div>
500: <div class="ck-note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>SKIPPED is new in KS-684.</strong></td><td> Previously the banner
501:         rendered a strict PASSED/FAILED binary, so
502:         <code>API_TOKEN not found</code> turned
503:         <strong>four healthy suites</strong> — GDPR IDOR (KS-258), live
504:         integration (KS-416), anchoring integrity (KS-489-D) and state-machine
505:         preconditions (KS-478) — into <strong>FAILED</strong> on the 2026-08-24
506:         run, sending readers after defects that did not exist. </td></tr><tr><td>An unmet
507:         precondition is not a test result. </td></tr><tr><td>A SKIPPED suite now contributes
508:         <em>neither</em> a pass nor a failure to <code>OVERALL</code>, and each
509:         row carries its reason — the two skip causes (“no credentials
510:         configured” vs “the platform did not answer”) stay
511:         distinguishable because they need different remedies. </td></tr><tr><td>Counting a skip as
512:         a <em>pass</em> would be the opposite and worse error.
513:       </td></tr></table></div>

522: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-live"></span> Live</td><td><strong></strong></td><td>Live / completed — a suite or check that runs today (✅)</td></tr>

524: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-int"></span> Integration</td><td><strong></strong></td><td>Schemathesis Integration mode — anchoring integrity + stored-state invariants, Local · pre-merge + nightly (⏳, not a PR gate)</td></tr>

526: <tr><td><span class="ck-sw ck-fail"></span> Fail</td><td><strong></strong></td><td>Failure / blocked — build fails, investigation, critical risk</td></tr>

1030: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>Note on "Separate KS Instance":</strong></td><td> under the consolidated
1031:       build-once/fan-out topology each suite job boots its own fully-isolated
1032:       stack — unique <code>COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME</code>/<code>STACK_PREFIX</code>
1033: <em>and</em> a per-suite host-port offset, with each tool pointed at its
1034:       own gateway (each an isolated stack; the CI-only per-suite port numbers are
1035:       historical and are not slot ports). </td></tr><tr><td>Isolation then came from both the per-suite
1036:       ports and GitHub-hosted runners being single-tenant/ephemeral (one stack
1037:       per runner), not from a shared default port. </td></tr><tr><td>Locally, isolation is the
1038:       stack slot and every port is the slot-1 base + 100·(N−1).
1039:     </td></tr></table>
1040: <h2>8. Local Stack Slots — Running Four Configurations at Once (KS-666)</h2>
1041: <div class="diagram-container">
1042: <div class="diagram-title">
1043:         8a. A LOCAL run must name its slot (KS-1016, 2026-09-11)
1044:       </div>
1045: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
1046:         Every harness — Schemathesis, k6, Playwright, Akto and the shared
1047:         provisioning step — refuses to start against a
1048:         <strong>local</strong> target (<code>localhost</code>,
1049:         <code>127.0.0.1</code>, <code>[::1]</code>,
1050:         <code>host.docker.internal</code>) when neither
1051:         <code>SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> nor the platform-s alias
1052:         <code>STACK_SLOT</code> is set, and prints the command to run instead:
1053:       </td></tr></table>
1054: <pre>
1055: No stack slot named. Every LOCAL system-test run must say which Docker stack it targets
1056: (target: http://localhost:6882/api). Name the slot and run again, for example:
1057:   SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=&lt;n&gt; python3 scripts/run.py pr
1058:   or: systemTest/run-in-slot.sh &lt;n&gt; python3 scripts/run.py pr
1059: Remote targets need no slot; CI (CI=true) is exempt.</pre>
1060: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>Local only.</strong></td><td> A remote target carries no slot and is left
1061:         alone; CI is exempt because its isolated per-suite stacks are local by
1062:         construction and deliberately unslotted (<code>CI=true</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Before
1063:         this rule an unset slot meant slot 1 silently — another ticket's
1064:         stack on a shared machine. </td></tr><tr><td>Proven on slot 2: no slot → exit 2, 0
1065:         docker calls, nothing provisioned; <code>STACK_SLOT=2</code> →
1066:         1,759 requests to the slot-2 gateway (6882 + 100·(2−1)).
1067:       </td></tr></table>
1068: </div>
1069: <div class="diagram-container">
1070: <div class="diagram-title">
1071:         8. One ticket, one worktree, one stack, one set of results
1072:       </div>
1073: <pre class="mermaid">
1074: graph TD
1075:     W1["worktree ks-123<br/>STACK_SLOT=1"] --&gt; K1["platform-k slot 1<br/>gateway :6882"]
1076:     WN["worktree ks-456<br/>STACK_SLOT=N (N = 1–4)"] --&gt; KN["platform-k slot N<br/>gateway :6882 + 100·(N−1)"]
1077:     K1 --&gt; R1["results *-slot1<br/>k6 dash :5665"]
1078:     KN --&gt; RN["results *-slotN<br/>k6 dash :5665 + 100·(N−1)"]
1079:     R1 --&gt; OBS["ONE observability stack (KS-971)<br/>slot picker, not a copy per slot<br/>k6 series + Loki streams + Pushgateway groups carry slot=<br/>cAdvisor carries NO name on Docker Desktop:<br/>container panels get name+slot by joining secuura_container_name_info<br/>app /metrics not implemented on any slot"]
1080:     RN --&gt; OBS
1081:     W1 -.pairs with.-&gt; S1["platform-s slot 1<br/>app :5122"]
1082:     WN -.pairs with.-&gt; SN["platform-s slot N<br/>app :5122 + 100·(N−1)"]
1083:         </pre>
1084: </div>
1085: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Four slots per platform, and the numbering is shared with platform-s
1086:         (PS-622).</strong></td><td>
1087:       Every published port is the historic one plus
1088:       <code>100 × (N − 1)</code>, so
1089:       <strong>platform-s slot N and platform-k slot N pair up with no
1090:         configuration</strong>: platform-k slot N's gateway lands on
1091:       <strong>6882 + 100 × (N − 1)</strong>. platform-s exports
1092:       <code>STACK_SLOT</code>; platform-k reads
1093:       <code>SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code>
1094:       and falls back to it, so a single export in a worktree drives both
1095:       platforms. </td></tr><tr><td>Four is a deliberate ceiling — the two platforms first
1096:       collide at platform-s slot 9, where its PMA proxy (8081) meets platform-k
1097:       tokenomics (8881).
1098:     </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>⚠ The same four ports mean different things locally and in
1099:         CI.</strong></td><td>
1100:       Section 5 (historical, Actions retired 2026-08-27) gave each suite
1101:       — schemathesis, playwright, performance, akto — its own CI-only
1102:       port block because each CI job booted its own single-tenant stack on an
1103:       ephemeral runner. </td></tr><tr><td>Locally the ports are <em>per stack slot</em> (slot-1
1104:       base + 100·(N−1)), and every suite targets whichever
1105:       slot it was pointed at. </td></tr><tr><td>Reading a local port as a CI suite (or the
1106:       reverse) will attribute a result to the wrong thing.
1107:     </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>Every harness follows the slot, and every result names it.</strong></td><td>
1108:       Source <code>systemTest/slot-target.sh</code> and Schemathesis
1109:       (<code>SECUURA_BASE_URL</code>), Playwright (<code>GATEWAY_URL</code>),
1110:       Akto (<code>SECUURA_API_URL</code>, plus its own side-stack, mongo volume
1111:       and dashboard port) and the performance runner
1112:       (<code>PERF_BASE_URL</code>) all aim at the same stack. </td></tr><tr><td>Akto and the
1113:       performance runner used to default to <code>localhost:6882</code> on their
1114:       own, so a run silently tested slot 1 whichever slot was meant; since
1115:       KS-1386 an unslotted local run is refused instead — there is no
1116:       default URL.
1117:       <strong>Playwright is the exception since KS-682:</strong>
1118: <code>config/stackSlot.ts</code> reads
1119:       <code>SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> itself, derives the gateway, refuses a
1120:       malformed or out-of-range slot and a label naming another slot, writes
1121:       <code>results/playwright-report-&lt;ticket&gt;-&lt;ts&gt;-slot&lt;N&gt;</code>
1122:       behind a <code>results/latest-slot&lt;N&gt;</code> pointer, and serves the
1123:       report on 9324 + 100·(N−1). </td></tr><tr><td>Pinned by the unit suite in
1124:       <code>systemTest/playwright/tests-unit/</code> (292 cases on the Mac,
1125:       2026-09-10; 389 passing in 6.5 s, Mac, 2026-10-06) —
1126:       including a boundary suite: an explicit slot outside 1–4 derives no
1127:       port, a suffix that spells the slot any way but the wrapper's

1444:       9. Auth surface — connector tokens on the users routes (KS-564, KS-1402)
1445:     </h2>
1446: <div class="diagram-container">
1447: <div class="diagram-title">
1448:         9a. KS-1402 — <code>GET /api/users/lookup</code> accepts a connector
1449:         token (Kam ruling 2026-10-02, option (a))
1450:       </div>
1451: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What it pins.</strong></td><td> Platform S authenticates with an
1452:         <code>sk_</code> connector key, so its token is a
1453:         <code>type: 'connector'</code> token rather than an interactive access
1454:         token. </td></tr><tr><td>Before KS-1402 only <code>POST /api/users/stub</code> accepted
1455:         one (KS-564, Option A); <code>GET /api/users/lookup</code> still used
1456:         plain <code>authenticate()</code>, so every Platform-S transfer-custody
1457:         call 401'd and fell back. </td></tr><tr><td>Both routes now go through
1458:         <code>authenticateAccessOrConnector()</code>.
1459:         <strong>The token type is not the permission.</strong> The route's own
1460:         role/scope gate still runs afterwards, so <code>users:read</code> is the
1461:         effective gate on <code>/lookup</code>, and a cross-tenant lookup still
1462:         returns <strong>404</strong> — not 200-empty, so positive existence is
1463:         not readable from the response shape.
1464:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>The audit label is route-neutral, deliberately.</strong></td><td> The
1465:         connector-accepted log line read <code>users/stub: …</code>
1466:         unconditionally, so once a second route accepted connector tokens every
1467:         <code>/lookup</code> call would have written an audit line naming a
1468:         route it never touched. </td></tr><tr><td>It now carries
1469:         <code>route: req.baseUrl + req.path</code>.
1470:         <code>req.originalUrl</code> was rejected for this field because it
1471:         carries the query string: measured on
1472:         <code>GET /api/users/lookup?email=alice%40example.com</code>,
1473:         <code>req.originalUrl</code> is
1474:         <code>/api/users/lookup?email=alice%40example.com</code> while
1475:         <code>req.baseUrl + req.path</code> is <code>/api/users/lookup</code> —
1476:         so <code>originalUrl</code> would put the email address in the clear in
1477:         the audit log, which is the very thing <code>maskEmail()</code> exists
1478:         to prevent.
1479:       </td></tr></table>

1695: <h2>11. RFC 3161 Timestamp Token Verification (KS-1404)</h2>
1696: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What changed.</strong></td><td><code>services/timestamping</code> accepted
1697:       an <strong>unsigned</strong> timestamp token as valid. </td></tr><tr><td>The old
1698:       <code>verifyRealToken</code> walked the ASN.1 tree and returned
1699:       <code>valid: true</code> whenever <em>any</em> OCTET STRING equalled the
1700:       expected document digest — no signature check, no certificate chain,
1701:       no TSTInfo parse, no algorithm-OID check. </td></tr><tr><td>A second path accepted a JSON
1702:       <code>{"hash":"…"}</code>
1703:       token outright. </td></tr><tr><td>Both are closed.
1704:     </td></tr></table>
1705: <h3>11.1 The verification chain, in order</h3>
1706: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>KS-1404 ITEM 2 (Seat D 5th):</strong></td><td> the verifier binds the
1707:       signer certificate via <code>signingCertificate(V2)</code> and builds the
1708:       chain from the token's own certificates to a pinned root. </td></tr><tr><td>The signer is
1709:       selected by an <strong>exact</strong> <code>SignerIdentifier</code> match
1710:       — issuer+serial or <code>subjectKeyIdentifier</code> — and the
1711:       previous <code>?? certs[0]</code> fallback is gone, so a token whose
1712:       <code>SignerInfo</code> names nothing it carries is refused rather than
1713:       checked against whichever certificate happened to be first. </td></tr><tr><td>The token's
1714:       other certificates are passed to the chain engine as
1715:       <strong>untrusted intermediates</strong>;
1716:       <code>trustedCerts</code> remains the configured anchors alone, so
1717:       carrying an intermediate can never create trust.
1718:       <code>rsaEncryption</code> (digest taken from
1719:       <code>digestAlgorithm</code>) and <code>RSASSA-PSS</code> (parameters
1720:       <strong>parsed, never defaulted</strong>) are accepted, because those are
1721:       the algorithms the pinned providers measurably use.
1722:     </td></tr></table>
1723: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>A defect of this PR, found and fixed inside it, and the cell that
1724:         caught it.</strong></td><td>
1725:       The first version of the chain fix passed
1726:       <code>certs: [signer, ...intermediates]</code>. pkijs treats the
1727:       <strong>LAST</strong> element of <code>certs</code> as the end-entity
1728:       — its own documented example is
1729:       <code>certs: [rootCa, intermediateCa, leafCert]</code> — so an
1730:       <em>intermediate</em> was validated as the leaf, and a token whose signer
1731:       chained to nothing was ACCEPTED whenever some certificate it carried
1732:       chained to an anchor. </td></tr><tr><td>The order is now
1733:       <code>[...intermediates, signer]</code>.
1734:       <strong>CHAIN-3 is the only cell that fails on the reversed order, and it stays
1735:         in the suite for that reason.</strong>
1736: </td></tr></table></div>
1737: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Strict DER</strong></td><td>definite, minimal lengths, nothing
1738:         trailing. </td></tr><tr><td>BER indefinite-length encoding is refused: a genuine token
1739:         re-wrapped as <code>30 80 … 00 00</code> was accepted before this
1740:         change.
1741:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>ContentInfo</strong></td><td> is <code>id-signedData</code>; SignedData's
1742:         <code>eContentType</code> is <code>id-ct-TSTInfo</code>.
1743:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>TSTInfo is parsed</strong></td><td>, and the message imprint is read from
1744:         <code>messageImprint.hashedMessage</code> — never searched for in
1745:         the tree.
1746:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>Exactly one SignerInfo</strong></td><td>, whose signed attributes carry
1747:         <code>contentType = id-ct-TSTInfo</code> and
1748:         <code>messageDigest = digest(eContent)</code>.
1749:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>The signature</strong></td><td> over the signed attributes re-encoded as
1750:         <code>SET OF</code>, against the signer certificate's public key.
1751:       </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>The signer certificate</strong></td><td> carries EKU
1752:         <code>id-kp-timeStamping</code>, is valid at <code>genTime</code>, and
1753:         <strong>chains to a configured trust anchor</strong>.
1754:       </td></tr></table>
1755: <h3>11.2 Fail-closed, and what that means operationally</h3>
1756: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
1757:       Trust anchors come from <code>TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM</code> (PEM text, or a
1758:       path to a bundle), committed as config.
1759:       <strong>Unset or empty means every real DER token verifies
1760:         <code>false</code></strong>
1761:       with reason <code>no trust anchor configured</code>. </td><td>Stored tokens
1762:       continue to verify through the database-row branch (same hash and
1763:       byte-identical proof), which this change does not touch.
1764:       <strong>Compose and per-environment wiring landed in KS-1404's second half and
1765:         is described in 11.4</strong>; this sentence previously read “Compose and per-environment wiring
1766:       is a separate step, so which environments have an anchor in effect is not
1767:       covered here”, which was true of #1376 and is now false.
1768:     </td></tr></table>

2094: <h2>12. GET /api/anchors/:id reports blockNumber as a number (KS-1333)</h2>
2095: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What this pins.</strong></td><td><code>services/originate/src/services/anchorStateSync.ts</code> has
2096:       <strong>four</strong> writers that persist
2097:       <code>blockHeight: anchor.blockNumber || 0</code> without shaping the
2098:       value, and <code>anchor.blockNumber</code> arrives from
2099:       <code>GET /api/anchors/:id</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>KS-1333's first step is to
2100:       <em>measure</em> whether that route can hand them a raw <code>pg</code>

2102:       <code>rowToAnchor</code> converts <code>block_number</code> through
2103:       <code>Number()</code> (<code>services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1317</code>),
2104:       and the handler answers the mapped
2105:       <code>anchor.blockNumber || null</code> rather than the raw row. </td></tr><tr><td>So the
2106:       route answers a number or <code>null</code>, and the ticket's own rule

2111: <h3>12.1 The cells, and why the guard is source-text</h3>
2112: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
2113:       Three cells in
2114:       <code>services/anchoring/src/__tests__/ks1333-get-by-id-blocknumber-is-a-number.test.ts</code>. <code>index.ts</code> calls <code>app.listen</code> at import, so no
2115:       test imports it; the guard therefore reads <code>index.ts</code> as
2116:       <strong>text</strong> over the two lines that make the answer a number.
2117:       <strong>B1</strong> pins the <code>Number()</code> conversion in
2118:       <code>rowToAnchor</code>. <strong>C1</strong> pins that the handler
2119:       answers the mapped value and never <code>row.block_number</code>.
2120:       <strong>C2</strong> pins that the by-id lookup maps its row through
2121:       <code>rowToAnchor</code> at all — without C2, B1 could pass while
2122:       the handler read a different row path entirely.
2123:     </td></tr></table>

2361: <h2>15. /revoke is one atomic transition (KS-1278)</h2>
2362: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What this pins.</strong></td><td><code>POST /api/documents/:id/revoke</code> decided
2363:       “already revoked” on a <strong>READ</strong>
2364:       (<code>routes/documents.ts:2374</code>) and then ran an <strong>unconditional</strong>
2365: <code>UPDATE</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>Two overlapping revokes could both pass that read, so both answered
2366:       <strong>200</strong>, both wrote an <code>action_provenance</code> row and both emitted an
2367:       anchor call. </td></tr><tr><td>The decision now lives <strong>IN the UPDATE</strong>:
2368:       <code>updateDocument</code> takes an <code>ifStatusIsNot</code> option that adds
2369:       <code>AND (${guardStatus}::text IS NULL OR status IS DISTINCT FROM
2370:       ${guardStatus}::text)</code> to the <code>WHERE</code>, and a guarded write that changed
2371:       <strong>no row</strong> returns <code>null</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>The loser of the race answers the
2372:       <em>same</em> <strong>400 BAD_REQUEST “Document is already revoked”</strong> as a
2373:       sequential caller, and returns <em>before</em> <code>recordOnBehalfOf</code> — so it
2374:       records <strong>no</strong> provenance row and emits <strong>no</strong> anchor.
2375:     </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Scope.</strong></td><td> This completes the ticket’s scope — the atomic
2376:       transition, the 400 for the loser, and provenance and anchor only for the winner. </td></tr><tr><td>The PR
2377:       says <code>Refs KS-1278</code>, not <code>Closes</code>. <strong>The row-lock alternative is
2378:       not taken.</strong>
2379: </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>What a <code>null</code> from the guarded write means, and what each meaning is
2380:       pinned by.</strong></td><td><code>updateDocument</code> already returned <code>null</code> for a
2381:       <em>missing</em> document (<code>documentRepo.ts:543</code> at
2382:       <code>4a1620588819</code>; <code>:538</code> at the branch base <code>32e058975d4e</code>),
2383:       so <code>null</code> is not a single condition and the route must not read it as one. </td></tr><tr><td>On the
2384:       guarded path it can arise three ways:
2385:     </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>A genuine race</strong></td><td>another revoke changed the row between this
2386:         request's read and its write. </td></tr><tr><td>The write refuses in the UPDATE, so exactly one of two
2387:         overlapping writers wins. <em>Instrument:</em> cell <code>R1</code>, which also asserts
2388:         <strong>0</strong> anchor emissions on the losing path, not only 0 provenance rows. </td></tr><tr><td>The
2389:         guard itself is pinned by cell <code>R2</code>, which asserts the guard clause by
2390:         <strong>exact text</strong> and the guard’s own two parameters <strong>by
2391:         position</strong> — a weaker assertion on either half is satisfied by a vacuous
2392:         guard, or by the <code>SET</code> clause’s new status standing in for the guard
2393:         value.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>The row was deleted inside the window</strong></td><td>the answer is 400 where
2394:         404 belongs. </td></tr><tr><td>This is <strong>unchanged by round 2</strong> and is tracked as
2395:         <code>KS 1419</code>. <em>Instrument:</em> none live — <strong>unmeasured</strong>
2396:         against a real database.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1"><strong>A revoke addressed by the platform UUID</strong></td><td><em>fixed in round 2.</em>
2397:         Both reads fall back to the primary key for a UUID-shaped id
2398:         (<code>documentRepo.ts:244-251</code>) and the API hands clients that key as
2399:         <code>documentUuid</code> (<code>:172</code>), but the guarded UPDATE keyed on
2400:         <code>external_id</code>. <strong>At the branch base and at round 1</strong> a sequential,
2401:         non-race revoke of a live, owned, unrevoked document addressed that way matched 0 rows and
2402:         answered <code>400 "Document is already revoked"</code> with 0 provenance rows and the
2403:         status never written. <strong>At round 2</strong> the guarded write keys on the row the read
2404:         resolved (<code>:616</code>, mirroring the read's own precedence: <code>external_id</code>
2405:         first, then the primary key), so it answers <code>200</code>, writes the status and records
2406:         exactly one provenance row. <em>Instrument:</em> cell <code>N1</code>, red at
2407:         <code>4a1620588819</code> and green at the round-2 head.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">
2408:       The route still 404s at <code>:2367</code> and 403s at <code>:2371</code> before the write, so
2409:       a missing or unowned document never reaches it. <strong>Only the opted-in revoke path changed
2410:       key</strong>: the other 12 production <code>updateDocument(</code> callers pass no
2411:       <code>ifStatusIsNot</code> and take a byte-identical statement
2412:       (<em>instrument:</em> cell <code>N3</code>). </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">A non-UUID external id never reaches the
2413:       <code>::uuid</code> cast, which would otherwise raise 22P02 (<code>:590</code>;
2414:       <em>instrument:</em> cell <code>N2</code>, green at both ends). </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">The remaining residual cases
2415:       are recorded under <em>Not covered</em> below.
2416:     </td></tr></table>

2595: <h2>
2596:       18. OAuth app scopes are a closed vocabulary, and the by-id routes are
2597:       owner-or-admin (KS-1210)
2598:     </h2>
2599: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> Any authenticated user, whatever their
2600:       role, could register an OAuth app — or change another user's app
2601:       — with <em>any</em> scope list at all, including the wildcard
2602:       <code>*</code>, the privileged <code>subjects:erase</code>, and strings
2603:       that are not scopes (<code>made:up</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Both request schemas took
2604:       <code>z.array(pgSafeStringSchema)</code>, i.e. any NUL-free string, and
2605:       neither <code>POST /apps</code> nor <code>PATCH /apps/:id</code> carried a
2606:       role or ownership check. </td></tr><tr><td>Measured again at this change's base:
2607:       <code>updateApp(id, updates)</code> and <code>getAppById(id)</code> are
2608:       keyed on the id ALONE, with no owner predicate — which answers a
2609:       question KS-1210 itself listed as not measured, and is why the gate
2610:       belongs in the route handlers rather than the repository.
2611:     </td></tr></table>
2612: <h3>
2613:       18.1 Two gates, two lists, and why they are copied rather than imported
2614:     </h3>
2615: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Gate 1</strong></td><td> closes both schemas to the <strong>nine</strong>
2616: <code>AVAILABLE_SCOPES</code>
2617:       (<code>services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:57-67</code>, blob
2618:       <code>8995edec6a43</code>): anything else is
2619:       <strong>400 for every caller</strong>, which alone closes the sev-5. </td></tr><tr><td>On
2620:       top of that, the privileged set <code>{admin:read, admin:write}</code> may
2621:       only be registered by a caller in the <strong>four</strong>-role platform
2622:       list — otherwise <strong>403</strong>. <strong>Gate 2</strong> makes
2623:       the four by-id routes (<code>GET</code>, <code>PATCH</code>,
2624:       <code>DELETE</code>, <code>POST .../rotate-secret</code>) answer
2625:       <strong>404</strong> unless the caller created the app or is in the
2626:       <strong>six</strong>-role admin list — 404 rather than 403, so
2627:       another user's app is not disclosed by the status code.
2628:     </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">
2629:       Neither list is importable: <code>PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES</code> is a
2630:       module-level const that is not exported (<code>routes/users.ts:192</code>)
2631:       and <code>ADMIN_ROLES</code> is local to that file's
2632:       <code>GET '/'</code> handler (<code>routes/users.ts:439</code>), both blob
2633:       <code>ea9f8da97a04</code>. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">They are therefore copied into
2634:       <code>routes/oauth.ts</code> by name, with a
2635:       <strong>drift cell</strong> that reads <code>users.ts</code> as source and
2636:       fails if either copy stops matching — so the duplication cannot rot
2637:       silently. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">An export edit in <code>users.ts</code> was deliberately not
2638:       made: that file belongs to other rows this round.
2639:     </td></tr></table>

2696: <h2>19. change-password reads the hash it verifies (KS-1005)</h2>
2697: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What changed.</strong></td><td><code>POST /api/users/me/change-password</code> answered
2698:       <strong>404 for every password account</strong>.
2699:       <code>services/auth/src/routes/users.ts</code> loaded the row with
2700:       <code>userRepo.getUserById</code>, whose column list (<code>userRepo.ts</code>
2701: <code>USER_COLS</code>, commented
2702:       <em>“All user columns EXCEPT password_hash”</em>) omits
2703:       <code>password_hash</code>; the next line throws
2704:       <code>NotFoundError('User')</code> on <code>!user.passwordHash</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>So
2705:       the hash was always absent and the endpoint was wholly non-functional
2706:       — not wrong at an edge. </td></tr><tr><td>It now calls
2707:       <code>getUserByIdWithPasswordHash</code>, the hash-carrying variant that
2708:       already existed and was used once, by <code>mfa.ts</code>, never here.
2709:       <strong>One call site changed; the other seven <code>getUserById</code> call
2710:         sites in the file are untouched.</strong>
2711: </td></tr></table>
2712: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>The defect was worse than “returns 404”.</strong></td><td> The
2713:       throw precedes <code>verifyPassword</code> entirely, so at base the route
2714:       answered 404 whether the current password was
2715:       <em>right or wrong</em> — it could not tell the two apart. </td></tr><tr><td>Cells A
2716:       and B pin exactly that asymmetry: A requires 200 for a correct password, B
2717:       requires <strong>400</strong>
2718:       for a wrong one. </td></tr><tr><td>Both were 404 before the change.
2719:     </td></tr></table></div>
2720: <h3>19.1 Why the cells mock the database and not the repository</h3>
2721: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2722:       The defect <em>is</em> the repository’s column list, so a cell that
2723:       stubbed <code>userRepo.getUserById</code> to hand back a
2724:       <code>passwordHash</code> would have mocked the defect away and passed on
2725:       broken code. </td><td>These cells run the <strong>real</strong> repository, routes,
2726:       error handler and argon2/bcrypt password service, and mock only
2727:       <code>../db</code>. The mock is faithful on the one property that decides
2728:       the outcome: it returns <code>password_hash</code>
2729: <strong>only when the SELECT actually named that column</strong>, exactly
2730:       as Postgres would. Cell C pins the mechanism directly — at base
2731:       <strong>zero</strong> SELECTs asked for <code>password_hash</code>.
2732:     </td></tr></table>

2828: <h2>20. Clearing MFA NULLs the TOTP seed and the hashed backup codes, at all three sites (KS-938)</h2>
2829: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> “MFA disabled” left the TOTP seed and the hashed
2830:       backup codes in the row. </td></tr><tr><td>The flag flipped, the call answered <strong>200 “MFA disabled
2831:       successfully”</strong>, and the credential material survived — so a seed could be
2832:       re-armed by <code>POST /api/users/me/mfa/verify</code>, which re-arms on the existing
2833:       <code>user.mfaSecret</code> without minting a new one. </td></tr><tr><td>The case that matters is the user who
2834:       disabled MFA <em>because</em> the authenticator was compromised.
2835:     </td></tr></table>
2836: <h3>20.1 The mechanism, and the one thing deliberately NOT changed</h3>
2837: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2838: <code>userRepo.updateUser</code> builds its SET list with
2839:       <code>if (tsField in updates &amp;&amp; updates[tsField] !== undefined)</code>.
2840:       <code>mfa_secret</code> and <code>mfa_backup_codes</code> <em>are</em> in
2841:       <code>fieldMap</code>, so the map was never the problem — the <strong>value</strong>
2842:       guard was. </td><td>All three clearing sites passed <code>undefined</code>, so a <strong>partial</strong>
2843:       UPDATE landed naming only the fields that survived.
2844:       <strong>The <code>undefined</code> skip is NOT changed</strong>: every other caller relies on it
2845:       to mean “leave this column alone”. <code>null</code> passes the guard and writes SQL
2846:       NULL, and the encryption branch guards on <code>typeof val === 'string'</code>, so a
2847:       <code>null</code> can never enter it. The codebase already knew the rule —
2848:       <code>wallet.ts</code> carries “null, NOT undefined” for
2849:       <code>walletAddress</code> (KS 720).
2850:     </td></tr></table>
2851: <h3>20.2 Three sites, and why the fix is per-site rather than one shared edit</h3>
2852: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
2853:       Addressed by <strong>symbol</strong>, with blobs, because the line numbers move: at this
2854:       change's base <code>routes/mfa.ts</code> is blob <code>87d3ee1079fe</code> and
2855:       <code>routes/users.ts</code> is blob <code>ea9f8da97a04</code>.
2856:       <code>mfa.ts</code> setup-verify <strong>revert</strong> (<code>updateUser</code>) and
2857:       <code>mfa.ts</code> <code>POST /mfa/disable</code> (<code>updateUserOrThrow</code>) each passed
2858:       <code>undefined</code> for both columns. <code>users.ts</code>
2859: <code>POST /me/mfa/disable</code> did <strong>not pass <code>mfaBackupCodes</code> at
2860:       all</strong>, so that site needed the <strong>key added</strong>, not merely re-valued —
2861:       which is why no single shared edit could have fixed all three.
2862:     </td></tr></table>
2863: <h3>20.3 Red-first, by assertion</h3>
2864: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
2865:       The cells drive the <strong>real route handlers over real loopback HTTP</strong> with the real
2866:       <code>userRepo</code> and the real <code>updateUser</code>, stubbing only <code>../db</code> so
2867:       the emitted statement can be captured, and they assert the <strong>SQL</strong> — not the
2868:       source text, which would still pass if the fix were commented out. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">At the base the three site
2869:       cells fail and the two controls pass (<strong>3 failed | 2 passed (5)</strong>); at the head
2870:       <strong>5 passed (5)</strong>. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Both numbers are non-zero, so the red is a real red and not a
2871:       load failure. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">The base failure quotes the defect verbatim:
2872:       <code>UPDATE users SET mfa_enabled = $1, verification_level = $2, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $3</code>.
2873:       </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">The load-bearing control drives the same real <code>updateUser</code> with
2874:       <code>undefined</code> and requires the two columns to be <strong>absent</strong> — a cell
2875:       that cannot tell the fix from its own fallback is not a regression test.
2876:     </td></tr></table>
2877: <h3>20.4 Residue, named and NOT fixed here</h3>
2878: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2879: <code>users.ts</code> <code>POST /me/mfa/disable</code> verifies the TOTP only
2880:       <code>if (user.mfaSecret &amp;&amp; ...)</code>, so an account with no stored seed disables MFA
2881:       with no proof of possession at all. </td><td>That is a separate defect in the same handler and is left
2882:       for its own ticket rather than widened into this one.
2883:     </td></tr></table>
2884: <h3>20.5 Running it</h3>
2885: <pre><code>cd Blockchain/Dev/services/auth
2886: npx vitest run src/__tests__/ks938-mfa-disable-nulls-seed-and-backup-codes.test.ts   # 5 cells
2887: npx vitest run                                                                       # 845 tests</code></pre>
2888: <h2>21. An unreadable connector allow-list refuses the create with 503 instead of granting everything (KS-1256)</h2>
2889: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="5"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> The connector allow-list is read out of platform settings to
2890:       decide whether a caller may create a restricted document type. </td></tr><tr><td>When that read failed, the parse
2891:       left <code>connectorConfig = {}</code> — and an empty config reads as
2892:       <strong>no restriction</strong>. </td></tr><tr><td>So every restricted connector became <em>unrestricted</em>
2893:       precisely when the platform could not tell what the restrictions were. </td></tr><tr><td>This is the same
2894:       fail-open class KS-1233 closed for the TTL trigger, still open on this path. </td></tr><tr><td>The read now
2895:       <strong>fails closed</strong>: an unreadable allow-list answers
2896:       <strong>503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE</strong> and the create is refused until the configuration can
2897:       be read.
2898:     </td></tr></table>
2899: <h3>21.1 The four outcomes, stated as a contract</h3>
2900: <table>
2901: <tr><th>State</th><th>Before</th><th>After</th></tr>
2902: <tr><td>the read THROWS (client <code>MaxRetriesPerRequestError</code>, or <code>JSON.parse</code> on malformed stored bytes)</td>
2903: <td>swallowed by a bare <code>} catch {}</code> → no restriction</td><td><strong>503</strong>, create refused</td></tr>
2904: <tr><td>Redis UNAVAILABLE</td><td>no restriction</td><td><strong>503</strong>, and the read is <em>never performed</em></td></tr>
2905: <tr><td>Redis available, the settings key ABSENT</td><td>no restriction</td><td><strong>no restriction — deliberately unchanged</strong></td></tr>
2906: <tr><td>the allow-list container is MALFORMED</td><td>403</td><td>403, unchanged (KS-1231)</td></tr>
2907: </table>
2908: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2909:       The third row is a decision, not an oversight. </td><td>It was put to Kam as
2910:       <code>secuura-connector-allowlist-missing-setting-ks1256-1005</code> and ruled <strong>b,
2911:       “Keep ‘no restriction’ when unset”</strong>, with the detail “No
2912:       behaviour change; the gap stays for fresh installs.” A fresh install has no
2913:       platform-settings key, and failing closed there would refuse every connector create on a new
2914:       deployment.
2915:     </td></tr></table>
2916: <h3>21.2 Two unreadable paths that do NOT share a mechanism, and why a catch cannot close one of them</h3>
2917: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2918:       Driven against real <code>ioredis</code> 5.11.1 and a real TCP RESP server, not a mock. </td><td>In the
2919:       <strong>unavailable</strong> state <code>getNotificationSettings</code> resolves
2920:       <strong>null without throwing</strong> — it reads an empty in-memory store
2921:       (<code>services/redis.ts:671-678</code>). A <code>catch</code> never observes a resolved null,
2922:       so the availability test has to come <em>before</em> the read rather than inside the catch.
2923:       That is why the fix is two edits and not one.
2924:     </td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2925:       Separately, <code>fallbackMode</code> is set on a sustained runtime outage by
2926:       <code>retryStrategy</code> at <code>services/redis.ts:78</code>, which carries
2927:       <strong>no <code>NODE_ENV</code> guard</strong>. </td><td>Driven under
2928:       <code>NODE_ENV=production</code> the branch fires identically, so
2929:       <strong>production reached the fail-open state on a runtime blip despite refusing to START
2930:       without Redis</strong>. The production cell exists to pin that.
2931:     </td></tr></table>
2932: <h3>21.3 Red-first, by assertion</h3>
2933: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2934:       Six cells, all six green at head. </td><td>At base, <strong>4 of the 6 are RED</strong> — the two
2935:       <code>CONTROL</code> cells are green at base by design, because they pin behaviour this change
2936:       does <em>not</em> touch (403 on a malformed container, and a readable allow-list still
2937:       restricting). A control that reddens with the fix would be testing the fix, not guarding it.
2938:       Measured by Seat E 6th and carried forward unchanged.
2939:     </td></tr></table>
2940: <h3>21.4 One collateral test, re-pointed deliberately</h3>
2941: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2942: <code>ks1195</code> exists to test the <strong>no-Redis degrade path</strong>: it asserts
2943:       <code>isRedisAvailable() === false</code> as a precondition, then used to pin that a connector
2944:       create still answered <strong>201</strong> there. </td><td>Both promises cannot hold — fail-closed
2945:       and “201 while Redis is down” are contradictory. Two assertions were re-pointed to
2946:       <code>[503, 503, 429, 429, 429]</code> and <code>toBe(0)</code>, and that cell's title now
2947:       states the new contract. <strong>These are the only assertion changes in this work.</strong>
2948:       The <code>DEGRADED</code> / <code>redis-not-ready</code> assertions are untouched.
2949:     </td></tr></table>
2950: <h3>21.5 What this costs, and whose decision it was</h3>
2951: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2952:       The cost is stated rather than discovered: <strong>while Platform K’s Redis is down,
2953:       Platform S cannot create documents through a connector</strong> — they answer 503. </td><td>That
2954:       was put to Kam as <code>secuura-ks1256-redis-outage-stops-connector-creates-1006</code> and
2955:       ruled <strong>a, “Accept: fail closed (503) during a Redis outage”</strong>:
2956:       “Security first: no restricted document type slips through while the allow-list cannot be
2957:       read. Cost: Platform-S cannot create documents while K’s Redis is down.”
2958:     </td></tr></table>
2959: <h3>21.6 Residue, named and NOT fixed here</h3>
2960: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
2961:       The <strong>other readers of the same settings key were not audited</strong>:
2962:       <code>admin.ts:1119</code>, <code>:1144</code>, <code>:1154</code>,
2963:       <code>health.ts:52</code> and <code>verification.ts:1283</code>. </td><td>Each may carry the same
2964:       fail-open shape. They are named here so the gap is on the record, not widened into this ticket.
2965:       The fresh-install gap in 21.1 row 3 stays open by Kam’s ruling b.
2966:     </td></tr></table>

3123: <h2>24. A missing GENERATED Prisma client is diagnosed, not reported as a module error (KS-1305)</h2>
3124: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> A fresh worktree installs <code>@prisma/client</code> but never
3125:       <em>generates</em> it: <code>npm ci</code> runs with <code>--ignore-scripts</code>, so
3126:       <code>prisma generate</code> does not run. </td></tr><tr><td>The bare <code>require('@prisma/client')</code> inside
3127:       <code>getPrismaClient()</code> then throws <code>Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default'</code>
3128:       — a module-resolution error that reads like a product defect in the originate service, and
3129:       which cost real time to diagnose more than once. </td></tr><tr><td>The load now names the cause and the command that
3130:       fixes it, and every other load error is rethrown untouched.
3131:     </td></tr></table>
3132: <h3>24.1 The mechanism, and what is deliberately NOT changed</h3>
3133: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3134:       The change is a <strong>pure insertion</strong> of 19 lines (<code>numstat 19 0</code>) immediately
3135:       before the existing <code>require</code>. </td><td>It loads <code>@prisma/client</code> once inside a
3136:       <code>try</code>; on success the original <code>require</code> reads the module cache, so the happy
3137:       path is byte-for-byte the same behaviour. <code>db.ts</code> is the <strong>tenant-isolation
3138:       module</strong> — it holds <code>withTenant</code>, the GUC wrapper, <code>getGucPrisma</code>
3139:       and <code>createPoolProxy</code> — and <strong>no GUC, tenant or RLS line is touched</strong>.
3140:       The six KS 458 tenant-GUC cells are green at the head. The new message carries no environment or
3141:       credential data; <code>cause</code> carries the resolver's error, which holds module paths only.
3142:     </td></tr></table>

3146:       contains <code>.prisma/client</code>; anything else is <code>throw err</code> — the
3147:       <strong>same object</strong>, not a copy. </td><td>A guard with three terms needs three arms, or some term is
3148:       being asserted by prose rather than by a cell.
3149:     </td></tr></table>

3210: <h2>27. The tenant-isolation job's stderr goes to its own file, so a legitimate run's artefact stays parseable (KS-1436)</h2>
3211: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> <code>Blockchain/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh:71</code> ran its
3212:         runner as <code>&gt; "$OUT" 2&gt;&amp;1</code>, folding <strong>stderr into the same file as the JSON
3213:         result</strong>. </td></tr><tr><td>The runner writes its result to stdout
3214:         (<code>tests/tenant-isolation/runner.ts:262</code>) and its diagnostics to stderr
3215:         (<code>runner.ts:74</code>, <code>console.error("login failed for …")</code>), so any stderr line
3216:         corrupted the artefact. </td></tr><tr><td>This is reached on a <em>routine</em> run, not an error path:
3217:         <code>runner.ts:150-151</code> is a deliberate two-principal fallback
3218:         (<code>verifier@</code> <code>||</code> <code>holder@</code>), and whenever the first login cannot
3219:         succeed the <code>console.error</code> line is emitted and the fallback proceeds as designed. </td></tr><tr><td>The job
3220:         still exited 0, while <code>:74</code> and <code>:75</code> read the artefact through
3221:         <code>jq … 2&gt;/dev/null || echo "?"</code> — so the parse failure was swallowed and the
3222:         job printed <code>tested=? cross-tenant_findings=?</code>.
3223:       </td></tr></table>
3224: <h3>27.1 Why it had to land before the aggregator change</h3>
3225: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3226:         Before KS 1136's change an unreadable artefact was reported as a <strong>clean</strong> scan, so a
3227:         genuine cross-tenant finding on a fallback run read as no findings. </td><td>After KS 1136 lands the aggregator
3228:         reports the artefact as unreadable instead, which turns every routine <code>verifier@</code>-fallback
3229:         run <strong>red with a false cause</strong>. That is why this one-line fix is the merge condition for
3230:         that pull request and lands first. KS 1382 is a <em>different</em> line in the same file
3231:         (<code>:31</code>, <code>TARGET_BASE</code> defaulting to slot 1's gateway) and is not addressed here.
3232:       </td></tr></table>
3233: <h3>27.2 The change, and what is deliberately NOT changed</h3>
3234: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3235:         One product line: <code>2&gt;&amp;1</code> becomes <code>2&gt; "$OUT.stderr"</code>. </td><td>The stderr content
3236:         is <strong>kept</strong>, not discarded — it is the diagnostic that explains a fallback, and a
3237:         <code>2&gt;/dev/null</code> variant is driven as its own red arm below. The file's
3238:         <code>Writes:</code> header line (<code>:23</code>) is unchanged: the new sidecar is a diagnostic, not
3239:         a declared artefact. The <code>jq … || echo "?"</code> swallow at <code>:74</code>-<code>:75</code>
3240:         is left in place; this ticket fixes the cause, not that symptom.
3241:       </td></tr></table>

3255: <h2>28. A present but unparseable security artefact is reported, not read as a clean scan (KS-1136)</h2>
3256: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> <code>09-aggregate-report.sh</code> reads each job's artefact with
3257:       <code>jq -r … 2>/dev/null</code> (08 with a bare <code>jq</code>), so an artefact that
3258:       <em>exists</em> but does not <em>parse</em> — a job that aborted mid-write — yielded zero

3260:       guarded 04's artefact; every other job's block was silent. </td></tr><tr><td>Each present, unparseable artefact now

3263: <h3>28.1 The mechanism, and what is deliberately NOT changed</h3>
3264: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">

3267:       <code>$TMP</code>, so the new findings are in the aggregate rather than appended after it. </td><td>It loops the
3268:       seven unguarded jobs (01 02 03 05 06 07 08) and calls the file's existing <code>emit</code>. 04 is

3422: <h2>25. A child vitest&rsquo;s verdict comes from its spawn outcome and its JSON report, never from its text (KS-1313)</h2>
3423: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="5"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> <code>childSuiteCounts</code> read the child run&rsquo;s totals by matching
3424:       <code>/Tests\s+(?:(\d+) failed \| )?(\d+) passed \((\d+)\)/</code> against the child&rsquo;s
3425:       <em>human-readable</em> stdout and stderr. </td></tr><tr><td>That pattern <strong>requires the word
3426:       &ldquo;passed&rdquo;</strong>, so a real fail-only, skip-only or todo-only run matched nothing and the
3427:       helper threw &mdash; the KS 1226 residue this ticket records. </td></tr><tr><td>Worse, a child
3428:       <strong>killed by its own 180 s <code>spawnSync</code> timeout</strong> writes no summary at all, so
3429:       whether it was read as a pass depended on what else happened to be in its output (KS 1326). </td></tr><tr><td>The
3430:       helper now runs the child with <code>--reporter=json --outputFile.json=&lt;tmp&gt;</code> and reads
3431:       <code>numPassedTests</code> / <code>numFailedTests</code> from the report. </td></tr><tr><td>Before the report is
3432:       read at all, <code>endedNormally</code> refuses any child that did not end on its own &mdash; a spawn
3433:       error, a signal, or an exit status other than 0 or 1 &mdash; so a killed child <strong>cannot</strong>
3434:       read as a pass even beside a passing report.
3435:     </td></tr></table>
3436: <h3>25.1 Red-first, and the proof it is not a load failure</h3>
3437: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Measured at base <code>147ae442074c</code>.</strong></td><td>

3439:       <strong>rc 1, 7 failed | 3 passed (10)</strong>, and all seven reds are R1&ndash;R7. </td></tr><tr><td>The cells red
3440:       <strong>by assertion, not by a load error</strong>: each calls a <code>reader()</code> helper whose
3441:       first act is <code>expect(typeof countsFromSpawn).toBe('function')</code>, and <code>typeof</code> on an
3442:       undeclared identifier is the one JavaScript form that does not throw. Proved rather than assumed by
3443:       reading the JSON report&rsquo;s own totals: <strong>passed + failed = 10</strong>, so cells ran.
3444:       <strong>0 passed and 0 failed would have been a load failure and is explicitly not what happened.</strong>
