3513: <h2>30. The transfer reject handler refuses a wrong-typed signature instead of running the reject (KS-1435)</h2>
3514: <h3>30.1 What was wrong, and why a 200 was the worst possible answer</h3>
3515: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3516:       The published <code>TransferRejectRequest</code> declares <code>signature</code> as a string, but
3517:       <code>rejectTransferSchema</code> in <code>services/transfer/src/index.ts</code> did not declare it at
3518:       all. </td><td>Zod strips keys a schema does not name, so a <code>signature</code> of the wrong type was
3519:       not refused — it was <strong>silently discarded</strong>, the schema then validated, and the reject
3520:       <em>ran</em> with <strong>200</strong>. The caller gets a success for a request the published contract
3521:       says is invalid, and the rejection is recorded without the signature it believed it had sent. A
3522:       stripped field is worse than a rejected one precisely because nothing surfaces.
3523:     </td></tr></table>
3524: <h3>30.2 The fix is one declaration, and <code>optional()</code> is the load-bearing half</h3>
3525: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3526:       <code>signature: z.string().optional()</code>, added to <code>rejectTransferSchema</code>.
3527:       </td><td>Typed, so a non-string is now a validation error and the handler answers
3528:       <strong>400</strong>. <code>optional()</code> keeps the field <em>not required</em>, which is what the
3529:       contract says and what every existing caller relies on: making it mandatory would have reddened the
3530:       pre-existing reject cells that send no signature at all. The narrowing is the <em>type</em>, never the
3531:       presence.
3532:     </td></tr></table>
3533: <h3>30.3 Red-first, and the red is an assertion rather than a load failure</h3>
3534: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3535:       With the test hunk applied <strong>alone</strong> and the product file untouched at the base, the suite
3536:       gives <strong>rc 1, 2 failed | 77 passed (79)</strong>. </td><td>Both failures read
3537:       <code>AssertionError: expected 200 to be 400</code> — the defect reproduced by its own symptom, not a
3538:       module that would not import. That distinction is the point of running the test hunk first: a
3539:       compile-breaking tamper reds with <strong>0 passed and 0 failed</strong>, which is a load failure and
3540:       proves nothing about the guard. Here 77 cells still pass around the two that fail.
3541:     </td></tr></table>
3542: <table>
3543: <tr><th>Cell</th><th>Sends</th><th>Base (test only)</th><th>Head (test + fix)</th></tr>
3544: <tr><td>TR1 — an object signature is refused with 400 and the transfer stays pending</td>
3545: <td><code>signature: {}</code></td><td><strong>RED</strong>, <code>expected 200 to be 400</code></td>
3546: <td>green</td></tr>
3547: <tr><td>TR2 — a numeric signature is refused with 400</td>
3548: <td><code>signature: 42</code></td><td><strong>RED</strong>, <code>expected 200 to be 400</code></td>
3549: <td>green</td></tr>
3550: <tr><td>TRC1 <em>(control)</em> — a string signature is accepted and the reject runs</td>
3551: <td><code>signature: '0xabc123'</code></td><td><strong>green</strong></td><td>green</td></tr>
3552: </table>
3553: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">
3554:       TRC1 is green on <strong>both</strong> sides, proved by name rather than by arithmetic.
3555:       </td><td><code>vitest run -t 'TRC1'</code> reads <strong>1 passed | 78 skipped</strong>, rc 0, at the
3556:       base <em>and</em> at the head. A control that is only green on one side cannot tell a real narrowing
3557:       from a schema that started refusing everything, so TR1 and TR2 going red while TRC1 holds is what
3558:       attributes the red to the wrong <em>type</em> and not to the field's presence.
3559:     </td></tr></table>

4758: <h3>61.1 Why no cell was possible against the real hook</h3>
4759: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>The behaviour is unobservable on the shipped hook.</strong></td><td> On <code>.githooks/pre-push</code> the only <code>${NAME:-</code> match is live code at <code>:77</code> (<code>if [ "${ALLOW_FORCE:-0}" = "1" ]; then</code>), so excluding comment lines yields the <strong>identical</strong> derived set <code>[ALLOW_FORCE]</code>. With the filter present or absent the output is the same, which is exactly why G2 survived every one of the 68 cells. A cell therefore cannot be written against the real hook at all; it needs a hook that carries a commented control, and no fixture mode wrote one. </td></tr><tr><td> The new <code>commented</code> mode writes a hook with <strong>both</strong>: a comment line beginning with <code>#</code> that names a control the hook never reads, and the live <code>ALLOW_FORCE</code> read. The derived set must stay <code>[ALLOW_FORCE]</code>; with the filter gone it becomes <code>[ALLOW_FORCE FAKE]</code>, because the derivation ends in <code>sort -u</code> and <code>FAKE</code> sorts second. The commented line must <strong>start</strong> with <code>#</code>: that is what the filter keys on, and a <code>${NAME:-</code> inside a <em>trailing</em> comment is not excluded.
4760:     </td></tr></table>
4761: <h3>61.2 Two oracles, and why the behavioural one needs FAKE set</h3>
4762: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>The announcement alone would not have been enough.</strong></td><td> Oracle (a) is the line leg 14 prints: the derived set must read exactly <code>ALLOW_FORCE</code>, asserted as a whole line so an extra name, a missing name or a reworded line all fail. But this is leg 14 describing its own work, and that is precisely what the earlier mutant M3 (announce the controls, strip nothing) was able to fake while surviving the gate at 61/61. </td></tr><tr><td> Oracle (b) is read from the <strong>stripped</strong> side, in the shape KS 1643&rsquo;s Minor 2 established for <code>ALLOW_FORCE</code>: <code>FAKE=1</code> is placed in the caller&rsquo;s environment and the fixture stub suite must still see it, because a commented control is never added to <code>env_clear</code>. The stub reports its own environment, so this does not read leg 14&rsquo;s words. </td></tr><tr><td> <strong>Why (b) needs <code>FAKE</code> SET.</strong> <code>env -u</code> on a variable that is already unset is indistinguishable from not stripping it, so an unset probe reads <code>&lt;unset&gt;</code> on the real tree <em>and</em> under G2 and discriminates nothing. One cell asserts that vacuity directly &mdash; with <code>FAKE</code> unset the probe reads <code>&lt;unset&gt;</code> either way &mdash; so a later edit cannot quietly simplify the <code>FAKE=1</code> out of the arm above it and leave a dead test behind.

4785: <h2>63. generated_guard_restore keeps the suite's own exit status when a cleanup is chained in front of it (KS-1738)</h2>
4786: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this fixes.</strong></td><td> <code>systemTest/__tests__/support/generated_guard.sh</code>&rsquo;s <code>generated_guard_restore()</code> captures the suite&rsquo;s exit status as its FIRST statement (<code>local rc=$?</code>) so a failed restore can re-raise it. That works when the guard IS the EXIT trap. It does not work when a suite chains its own cleanup in front of it: the chained command runs first and overwrites <code>$?</code>. </td></tr><tr><td> <code>systemTest/__tests__/bootstrap_login_diagnosis.test.sh</code> did exactly that &mdash; <code>trap 'stop_stub; generated_guard_restore' EXIT</code>. <code>stop_stub</code> succeeds, so <code>$?</code> was 0 by the time the guard read it, the guard took its &ldquo;the suite itself passed&rdquo; branch, and a suite that exited 3 was reported as 1. <strong>LOW severity, and stated as such:</strong> a failed restore is still reported and still exits non-zero, and the runner still scores the suite as failed &mdash; only the distinction between &ldquo;the suite failed&rdquo; and &ldquo;the restore failed&rdquo; is lost. </td></tr><tr><td> <strong>The ticket listed three shapes and chose none.</strong> Shape 3 (&ldquo;leave it&rdquo;) was ruled out by Wednesday; shapes <strong>1 and 2 together</strong> were chosen by the builder and ratified. Shape 1 is the fix (an optional status argument), shape 2 is the constraint written down at the guard&rsquo;s header and at the chained call site &mdash; because the ticket&rsquo;s own risk statement is that chaining is the natural thing for the next suite to do.
4787:     </td></tr></table>
4788: <h3>63.1 The shape, and why the ticket's own suggested call-site form was NOT used</h3>
4789: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>Opt-in, so no existing caller changes behaviour.</strong></td><td> <code>generated_guard_restore</code> now PREFERS a status passed as its first argument over <code>$?</code>. <code>local rc=$?</code> stays the first statement &mdash; any command before it, <code>[</code> included, overwrites <code>$?</code> &mdash; and the argument is applied immediately after. With no argument the behaviour is byte-for-byte the old one, which is why the two inline copies and every plain-trap caller are untouched. </td></tr><tr><td> The chained call site becomes <code>trap 'rc=$?; stop_stub; generated_guard_restore "$rc"' EXIT</code>: the cleanup still runs FIRST, and the real status is handed in. <strong>The ticket&rsquo;s literal shape-1 suggestion was <code>trap 'generated_guard_restore $?; stop_stub' EXIT</code>, and that was deliberately not used:</strong> on a failed restore the guard <code>exit</code>s, so putting the guard first would mean <code>stop_stub</code> never runs on exactly the path the guard exists for &mdash; it would leak the login-stub listener that KS 1201 was filed about. That reasoning was put to Wednesday and ratified as reasoning; the gate judges whether the code does it. </td></tr><tr><td> A non-numeric argument is REFUSED by name and falls back to <code>$?</code>, rather than being used: <code>exit "$rc"</code> on a non-number is a shell error, which would trade a wrong status for no status at all. That branch has its own cell.
4790:     </td></tr></table>

4826: <h3>66.1 Why the old arm is kept, not replaced</h3>
4827: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Replacing <code>nocontrol</code> outright would have lost a kill.</strong></td><td> Before this change the non-empty arm was exercised by accident, through the misnamed fixture, and four existing cells depended on it. The old line is therefore kept verbatim as <code>trailingcomment</code> and given its own cells, which also pins a boundary of the filter that had no cell: a <code>${NAME:-</code> in a <em>trailing</em> comment is not excluded. </td></tr><tr><td> The three existing call sites of <code>nocontrol</code> (<code>HOOKCTL-REFUSED/1</code>, the short-circuit, and the KS-1643 withheld-run cells) now run on the arm their comments describe &mdash; &ldquo;the derivation has stopped working&rdquo; &mdash; and stay green at 82/0.

4829: <h3>66.2 The <code>-z</code> disjunct cannot be pinned, and why</h3>
4830: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>It is redundant, so deleting it is an equivalent mutant.</strong></td><td> For an empty set the second half of the condition is also true: <code>printf '%s\n' "" | grep -qx 'ALLOW_FORCE'</code> fails, and the <code>!</code> makes that a refusal. So <code>[ -z "$hook_controls" ] || &hellip;</code> and the same condition with the first half removed refuse on exactly the same inputs. A truth table over five derived sets (<code>[]</code>, <code>[NAME]</code>, <code>[ALLOW_FORCE]</code>, <code>[ALLOW_FORCE FAKE]</code>, <code>[FAKE]</code>) under bash 3.2 with <code>pipefail</code>, which is <code>preflight.sh:91</code>&rsquo;s own setting, gives identical columns for the original and the deletion. </td></tr><tr><td> Driven through the real suite as a matched pair, the deletion arm reads <strong>82 passed, 0 failed</strong> and a cell-by-cell verdict diff against the control moves <strong>zero cells</strong>. No cell can distinguish the disjunct&rsquo;s presence, so a cell that &ldquo;goes red when it is deleted&rdquo; cannot exist. What a cell can do is make the branch <em>execute</em>, which the empty arm now does, and pin the two mutants that are not equivalent. </td></tr><tr><td> <strong>The two killable mutants separate cleanly by arm.</strong> <code>M_accept</code> (an empty set is accepted: <code>[ -n "$hook_controls" ] &amp;&amp; ! &hellip;</code>) proceeds only on the empty set, and is killed by the empty arm. <code>M_2nd</code> (only <code>-z</code> remains) proceeds on <code>[NAME]</code> and <code>[FAKE]</code>, and is killed by the trailing-comment arm. Whether to delete the redundant disjunct from <code>preflight.sh</code> is a product-file question and is not decided here.
4831:     </td></tr></table>
4832: <h3>66.3 Red-first, and the figures</h3>
4833: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>Measured at base <code>b6366c12a8ab</code>, 2026-10-27, Kamil&rsquo;s MacBook Pro (Mac14,5, 12 cores).</strong></td><td> Node v26.8.1, npm 11.19.0, GNU bash 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin26), macOS 27.0.1. 4994: <h2>78. Five originate log-line describers can no longer take a request down: the fail500 helpers of four route files and the per-tenant catch of migrate-tenant-data (KS-1772)</h2>
4995: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this changes.</strong></td><td> KS-1772 names five places in <code>services/originate</code> where a log line was built from a thrown value with no <code>try</code> of its own, the shape PR 1754 fixed in api-gateway (KS-1524 (a)). The five are the <code>fail500</code> helper of <code>routes/systemErrors.ts</code>, <code>routes/gdpr.ts</code>, <code>routes/webhooks.ts</code> and <code>routes/adminConfig.ts</code>, and the per-tenant catch of <code>POST /api/admin/migrate-tenant-data</code> in <code>adminConfig.ts</code>. </td></tr><tr><td><strong>A behaviour change on request paths.</strong> A thrown value whose description throws (a <code>message</code> getter that throws, a Proxy whose <code>getPrototypeOf</code> or <code>ownKeys</code> trap throws, a revoked Proxy), or a logger that throws, made the describer throw from inside its own catch. In the four <code>fail500</code> helpers that rejected the async handler, Express 4 never sees a rejected promise, and the request got no response. In the per-tenant catch it escaped into the route&rsquo;s outer catch: the loop stopped at that tenant, later tenants were never tried, and the route answered 500 where its contract is a 200 whose <code>results</code> carries the failing tenant&rsquo;s code. </td></tr><tr><td>Each site now describes the value in its own <code>try</code> (fallback line <code>thrown value that could not be described</code>) and logs in another, so the constant 500, or the tenant&rsquo;s row and the next tenant, is always produced. For every value that could be described before, the log line is unchanged. The guards are written inline at each site and not as a shared helper: the per-tenant row <code>TENANT_COPY_FAILED</code>, its bare-string shape and a shared describer are KS-1462 item 2, and are not touched.

5049: <h2>81. api-client.ts declares the error body the gateway sends: a string or an object { code, message } at all three sites (KS-1767)</h2>
5050: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What this changes.</strong></td><td> KS-1767 records that the MCP server&rsquo;s <code>api-client.ts</code> typed a response&rsquo;s <code>error</code> as a string at three sites (<code>registerDocument</code>, <code>getWorkflowInstance</code>, <code>getConnectorInfo</code>) while the gateway&rsquo;s published error body carries an object <code>{ code, message }</code>. 5071: <h3>82.1 Why 500 and not 503</h3>
5072: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>There is no classifier in originate to reuse.</strong></td><td> auth classifies infrastructure faults with <code>isInfrastructureDbError</code> (<code>services/auth/src/repositories/dbErrors.ts</code>), which reads <code>pg</code> error codes (classes 08, 53, 57), socket error codes and <code>pg</code> pool messages. originate reads through Prisma (<code>prisma.$queryRaw</code>), whose errors carry other codes and other text, and a search of <code>services/originate/src</code> outside the tests finds no classifier and no service-unavailable error type (the 503 hits are OpenAPI declarations and the load-shedding mount in <code>index.ts</code>). A 503 here would mean writing and proving a new classifier for one route. The route&rsquo;s existing catch already answers a constant 500, which is inside Kam&rsquo;s ruling (&ldquo;500/503&rdquo;), and the coordinator accepted it: do not import auth&rsquo;s helper across services for this. </td></tr><tr><td>The other shape the ticket names, a discriminated result, was not chosen: it would carry one bit (fault or absence) through a single caller that already has a catch. Letting the error propagate changes one line and leaves null meaning one thing only.
5073:     </td></tr></table>

5114: <table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>The class hierarchy, not any service.</strong></td><td> The cells prove the prototype of an instance of each of the nine subclasses and of <code>DocumentNotFoundError</code> (a two-level subclass), that every instance is still an <code>AppError</code> and an <code>Error</code> with its status, and that <code>errorHandler</code> still answers a <code>ValidationError</code> with its details and a 422. The test imports the package by its source path; it runs no service. </td></tr><tr><td>Not measured: the suites of the other services that import these classes from <code>@secuura/shared</code> (only the packages/shared suite was run), the services/auth half of KS-1467, a running stack, the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, Performance/k6), a Node 24 LTS run, and any deploy. None of them is claimed as passing.
5115:     </td></tr></table>

980: <div style="font-size: 7.5px; color: var(--muted); margin: -3px 0 7px 0"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td colspan="2">
981:       Note:
982:       <strong>Schemathesis coverage below is read-path only (KS-428).</strong>
983:       The gateway's CSRF guard is <strong>inverted</strong> (it skips CSRF when
984:       no <code>Authorization</code> header is present and enforces it when one
985:       is), so every mutating request from a bearer-token client is rejected with
986:       <code>403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING</code> (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE alike), and
987:       <code>403</code> is an accepted status — so a sweep can report
988:       <em>0 failed</em> across all 344 operations without having exercised any
989:       create, update or delete path. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">The endpoint counts in the matrix are
990:       operations <em>attempted</em>, not write paths verified. </td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Treat a green
991:       Schemathesis run accordingly until KS-428 is resolved.

1931: <!-- When to combine + Common pitfalls -->
1932: <div class="bottom-grid">
1933: <div class="panel">
1934: <div class="panel-head ph-combine">
1935:           🧱 Stack slots — four configurations at once (KS-666)
1936:         </div>
1937: <div class="panel-body">
1938: <table class="pmatrix rmatrix"><tr><th>Item</th><th>Detail</th></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">No slot named?</td><td><strong>Refused, LOCAL only (KS-1016, 2026-09-11).</strong> Every
1939:               harness — Schemathesis, k6, Playwright, Akto and the shared
1940:               provisioning step — stops at start when the target is local
1941:               (<code class="cm">localhost</code>,
1942:               <code class="cm">127.0.0.1</code>, <code class="cm">[::1]</code>,
1943:               <code class="cm">host.docker.internal</code>) and neither
1944:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> nor the platform-s
1945:               alias <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code> is set, and prints the
1946:               command to run instead:
1947:               <pre class="cm">
1948: No stack slot named. Every LOCAL system-test run must say which Docker stack it targets
1949: (target: http://localhost:6882/api). Name the slot and run again, for example:
1950:   SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=&lt;n&gt; python3 scripts/run.py pr
1951:   or: systemTest/run-in-slot.sh &lt;n&gt; python3 scripts/run.py pr
1952: Remote targets need no slot; CI (CI=true) is exempt.</pre>
1953:               Remote targets (demo, a tunnel) carry no slot and are left alone;
1954:               CI is exempt because its isolated per-suite stacks are local and
1955:               deliberately unslotted (<code class="cm">CI=true</code> — a
1956:               convention, not a lock). </td></tr><tr><td>Before this rule an unset slot meant slot
1957:               1 silently.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3">Pick a slot</td><td><code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>Four slots; every published port is the historic one plus
1958:               <strong>100 × (N − 1)</strong>. </td></tr><tr><td>Gateway
1959:               <strong>6882 + 100 × (N − 1)</strong> (slot 1:
1960:               6882).</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">Pair with platform-s</td><td>The numbering is <strong>shared</strong> (PS-622): S slot N and K
1961:               slot N line up with no configuration. platform-s exports
1962:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code> and platform-k falls back to
1963:               it, so <strong>one export drives both</strong>.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Point the suites</td><td><code class="cm">source systemTest/slot-target.sh</code> —
1964:               Schemathesis, Playwright, Akto (with its own side-stack, mongo
1965:               volume and dashboard port) and the performance runner all follow.
1966:               </td></tr><tr><td>Akto and the performance runner used to default to
1967:               <code class="cm">localhost:6882</code> alone, so a run silently
1968:               tested slot 1; since KS-1386 an unslotted local run is refused
1969:               instead — there is no default URL.
1970:               <strong>Playwright is the exception since KS-682</strong>: it
1971:               reads <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> itself, derives
1972:               the gateway (6882 + 100·(N−1)), refuses a malformed
1973:               or out-of-range slot, and refuses a label naming a different slot
1974:               — unsourced
1975:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=&lt;n&gt; npx playwright test</code>
1976:               targets slot &lt;n&gt; or fails saying why, never slot 1 in
1977:               silence (KS-1056 tracks the other three).</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="6">Fresh local stack: the bootstrap admin</td><td>Every harness provisions its actors through
1978:               <code class="cm">fixtures/provision-actors.ts</code>, which grants
1979:               roles as <code class="cm">admin@secuura.com</code> using
1980:               <code class="cm">BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>That account
1981:               exists only if the auth seeder received
1982:               <code class="cm">ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD</code> at build time —
1983:               set it in <code class="cm">Blockchain/Dev/.env</code> (line 133 of
1984:               the template) <em>before</em>
1985: <code class="cm">start-secuura.sh --rebuild</code>, and export the
1986:               same value as <code class="cm">BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD</code> in
1987:               the shell that runs the suite. </td></tr><tr><td>Until 2026-09-10 the value was
1988:               never forwarded to the container, so it did nothing and every
1989:               fresh stack 401'd (KS-972); compose now forwards it (KS-682, from
1990:               KS-971) and <code class="cm">check-stack-safety.sh</code> refuses
1991:               a compose file that drops it. </td></tr><tr><td>If provisioning prints
1992:               <strong>DEGRADED</strong>, this is the first thing to check. </td></tr><tr><td>Since
1993:               2026-09-10 Playwright's <code class="cm">global-setup</code> hands
1994:               provisioning its own slot-derived gateway (<code class="cm">--base-url</code>), so an unsourced
1995:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N</code> run provisions on
1996:               slot N — before that it provisioned against slot 1 whatever
1997:               slot the suite ran on, DEGRADED when slot 1 was down, and
1998:               coincided silently when it was up (KS-682). </td></tr><tr><td>The manifest, its
1999:               rejected copy and any superseded copy all carry the slot segment
2000:               (<code class="cm">actors-slot&lt;n&gt;.superseded-&lt;ts&gt;.json</code>), so a quarantined manifest keeps its attribution.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="6">Schemathesis self-resolves</td><td><strong>KS-1016:</strong> Schemathesis no longer depends on that
2001:               export. </td></tr><tr><td>It reads <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> (or
2002:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code>) itself and derives the gateway
2003:               by the same
2004:               <strong>historic + 100 × (N − 1)</strong> rule, so
2005:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=&lt;n&gt;</code> alone targets
2006:               <code class="cm">:6882 + 100·(n−1)</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>One
2007:               resolver answers for the runner, the hooks and the persona logins
2008:               — they used to disagree, and a shell carrying only
2009:               <code class="cm">API_BASE_URL</code> sent the runner to one slot
2010:               and every login to another, inside a single run. </td></tr><tr><td>Edge cases
2011:               (padding, trailing slashes, a blank-but-present variable, a
2012:               whitespace <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> masking
2013:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code>) are pinned in
2014:               <code class="cm">tests/unit/test_slot_resolver_edges.py</code>;
2015:               the fixture, the compose project probe, the shell-executed slot
2016:               rule and the best-effort pushes each have their own module, and
2017:               the no-hardcoded-slot guard scans <code class="cm">src/</code>,
2018:               <code class="cm">scripts/</code> and
2019:               <code class="cm">config/</code> too. </td></tr><tr><td>Refuses what the shell
2020:               refuses (<code class="cm">0</code>, <code class="cm">01</code>,
2021:               <code class="cm">abc</code>, <code class="cm">5</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Proven by
2022:               rotation on slots 4, 3, 2 and 1, one at a time with the others
2023:               torn down and every <code class="cm">docker</code> call audited
2024:               (2026-09-10/11).</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3">API Explorer names its slot (KS-1386)</td><td>Generate with the slot:
2025:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N npm run generate --
2026:                 ../../Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml output/</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>The explorer's <strong>Local</strong> server, its two
2027:               health-check curls and its troubleshooting hints point at slot N's
2028:               gateway (<strong>historic + 100 × (N − 1)</strong>); a
2029:               local run that names no slot is refused — under CI too,
2030:               since the explorer has no URL of its own. </td></tr><tr><td>Until 2026-09-29 every
2031:               explorer pointed at slot 1, and because every explorer opened from
2032:               disk shares one browser-storage origin, a server chosen on one
2033:               slot's page was reused by another's — the page now ignores a
2034:               stored server it does not offer.
2035:               <code class="cm">src/config/stackSlot.ts</code> is the package's
2036:               copy of the shared slot rule, pinned to
2037:               <code class="cm">fixtures/slot.ts</code> by a parity test.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4">No slot named → refused, never slot 1 (KS-1386)</td><td>Every harness refuses a LOCAL run that names no slot (<code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code>
2038:               or <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code>), at every step that touches
2039:               a stack. <code class="cm">CI=true</code>/<code class="cm">1</code>/<code class="cm">yes</code> and remote targets need no slot, but
2040:               with no slot and no URL the run is refused — there is no
2041:               default URL. </td></tr><tr><td>An exempt run is labelled
2042:               <code class="cm">unslotted</code> (metrics, run metadata,
2043:               <code class="cm">actors-unslotted.json</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Name the slot:
2044:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=&lt;n&gt; npm run …</code> or
2045:               <code class="cm">systemTest/run-in-slot.sh &lt;n&gt; …</code>.
2046:               </td></tr><tr><td>Akto's and Performance's refusals name the npm script you ran, so
2047:               the command they show can be pasted back with the slot, e.g.
2048:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1 npm run test:pr</code>.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4">BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD on EVERY run</td><td>Export it in the shell of every suite run — Schemathesis's
2049:               <code class="cm">run.py</code> provisions actors too, not only the
2050:               TypeScript suites. </td></tr><tr><td>The FIRST provisioning on a fresh stack creates
2051:               the five generated actors; without the variable they are created
2052:               as <code class="cm">OWNER</code> (log:
2053:               <code class="cm">bootstrap admin: UNAVAILABLE</code>,
2054:               <code class="cm">+ … role=OWNER</code>) and every later run finds
2055:               them pre-existing, cannot re-role them, reports DEGRADED and
2056:               — for Playwright — fails auth-setup with a
2057:               <code class="cm">400</code> (KS-966: the admin password comes from
2058:               the manifest). </td></tr><tr><td>A retry does not fix it: reset that slot's DB
2059:               (<code class="cm">start-secuura.sh --fresh-db</code>) or use a new
2060:               <code class="cm">--seed</code>, then rerun the series with the
2061:               variable set. </td></tr><tr><td>Measured 2026-09-11 on slot 4 (KS-1016).
2062:               <strong>Since KS-1016 provisioning refuses</strong> when the
2063:               bootstrap admin is unavailable — nothing is created, the
2064:               pre-suite says DEGRADED and why, and the next run with the
2065:               variable set provisions correctly.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">DEGRADED names what happened to the manifest (KS-981)</td><td>When provisioning fails, any manifest on disk is moved aside
2066:               (<code class="cm">actors-slotN.superseded-&lt;ts&gt;.json</code>)
2067:               and the DEGRADED banner says which of three things happened:
2068:               <em>moved to &lt;path&gt;</em>, <em>none on disk</em>, or
2069:               <strong>could NOT be moved</strong> — the last naming the
2070:               file to check (<code class="cm">fixtures/generated/actors-slotN.json</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Since 2026-09-29 the strict arm (<code class="cm">SYSTEMTEST_REQUIRE_PROVISIONED=true</code>) says it too; before, it printed only <em>FATAL</em>, so a
2071:               manifest left on disk for the <em>next</em> run went unreported,
2072:               and the could-not-move advice named the old
2073:               <code class="cm">actors.json</code> that nothing reads.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4">Push refused: NOTHING CHECKED (KS-1063)</td><td>The pre-push hook always runs the
2074:               <code class="cm">systemTest/*</code>
2075:               format gate over the packages a push touches — for a
2076:               systemTest-only push it is the only gate that runs. </td></tr><tr><td>A package with
2077:               no deps installed is skipped and named. </td></tr><tr><td>Since 2026-09-29, if
2078:               <strong>every</strong> selected package is skipped the push is
2079:               refused with
2080:               <code class="cm">NOTHING CHECKED … This is NOT a formatting failure</code>: run <code class="cm">npm ci</code> in each package it names and
2081:               push again. </td></tr><tr><td>Before, it passed on
2082:               <code class="cm">0 package(s) checked, N skipped, 0 failed</code>
2083:               — indistinguishable from a clean check.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4">Login failure says WHICH cause (KS-1167)</td><td><strong>KS-1167 (2026-09-14):</strong> the shared pre-suite login
2084:               used to drop the HTTP status, so
2085:               <code class="cm">bootstrap admin: UNAVAILABLE</code> explained
2086:               every non-200 as “check the password” —
2087:               including a <strong>429 from the per-IP login limiter</strong>,
2088:               which had never looked at the password. </td></tr><tr><td>It now names the cause:
2089:               <em>unreachable</em> (with
2090:               <code class="cm">ECONNREFUSED &lt;host&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</code>
2091:               — was the bare <code class="cm">fetch failed</code>, the
2092:               port lost in <code class="cm">.cause</code>),
2093:               <em>limiter</em> (429: password NOT checked, wait the 15-minute
2094:               window), <em>rejected</em> (401/400/403: check
2095:               <code class="cm">ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD</code> / lockout),
2096:               <em>unexpected</em> (5xx or a token-less 200: gateway health).
2097:               </td></tr><tr><td>Playwright's <code class="cm">auth-setup</code> does the same for
2098:               its own login (<code class="cm">helpers/login-diagnosis.ts</code>:
2099:               limiter / EMPTY password from a withheld manifest / rejected /
2100:               unhealthy, each naming its next step), and its global-setup now
2101:               <strong>refuses on a 429 ping</strong> instead of proceeding into
2102:               provisioning inside a cooldown. </td></tr><tr><td>Pinned by
2103:               <code class="cm">__tests__/bootstrap_login_diagnosis.test.sh</code>
2104:               (a stub gateway answering one fixed status, plus a port proven
2105:               closed — no stack),
2106:               <code class="cm">performance/tests/unit/fixtures/{loginOutcome,describeError}.test.ts</code>
2107:               and the Playwright <code class="cm">login-diagnosis</code> /
2108:               <code class="cm">preflight-verdict</code> unit files.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4">Slot gate driven as a PROCESS; unit suites slot-independent
2109:               (KS-1167)</td><td>Playwright and k6 proved their KS-1016 guard was
2110:               <em>called</em> by reading the runner as text; Akto and
2111:               Schemathesis already spawned theirs. </td></tr><tr><td>Both now spawn the real entry
2112:               point too — and
2113:               <code class="cm">npm run report</code> (Playwright), which
2114:               resolved slot 1 silently, consults the rule (<code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1 npm run report</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>Separately,
2115:               <strong>the offline unit suites were not slot-independent</strong>: measured 2026-09-14, Playwright 348/348 unslotted but
2116:               345–347/348 from a slotted shell, Performance 1077/1077 vs
2117:               1060–1067 — files cleared the slot family only in
2118:               <code class="cm">afterEach</code>, never cleared the
2119:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code> alias, and k6's runner modules
2120:               freeze their slot at import. </td></tr><tr><td>Fixed (Playwright: clear before each
2121:               + a <code class="cm">childEnv()</code> strip for spawns;
2122:               Performance: a vitest <code class="cm">setupFiles</code> strip
2123:               before every file loads) and pinned by a matrix that re-runs the
2124:               suite under no slot and slots 1–4 (both variables, and the
2125:               wrapper's suffix shape) and demands identical counts.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">STACK_SLOT alias everywhere</td><td>Every slot reader (shared manifest writer, Playwright, k6, Akto,
2126:               Schemathesis) honours platform-s's
2127:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT</code> in
2128:               <code class="cm">stack_env.sh:37</code>'s order:
2129:               <code class="cm">SECUURA_STACK_SLOT</code> wins, a blank one falls
2130:               through, a malformed alias is refused. </td></tr><tr><td>A
2131:               <code class="cm">STACK_SLOT=N</code>-only shell used to drive slot
2132:               N's gateway while opening slot 1's actors (KS-1016,
2133:               2026-09-11).</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3">⚠ Cross-slot reads refused</td><td><strong>KS-1016:</strong> the DB sweeps and the compose
2134:               controller now refuse a stack slot other than the one the HTTP
2135:               assertions target, naming both sides. </td></tr><tr><td>Previously
2136:               <code class="cm">docker exec secuura-postgres</code> was
2137:               hardcoded, so a slot-3 run counted rows in
2138:               <strong>slot 1's</strong> database — and every slot shares
2139:               one Postgres password (KS-731), so the wrong database answered
2140:               rather than refusing. </td></tr><tr><td>The compose path was worse: it
2141:               <em>stops and recreates</em>, so it took another ticket's stack
2142:               down.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Run metrics per slot</td><td><strong>KS-1016:</strong> the Pushgateway grouping key carries
2143:               the slot (<code class="cm">/job/integration/environment/local/slot/&lt;n&gt;</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>There is one shared
2144:               <code class="cm">secuura-obs-pushgateway</code> on
2145:               <code class="cm">:9099</code>, and a same-key push
2146:               <em>replaces</em> the group — so two slots used to overwrite
2147:               each other's run summary and the survivor silently described
2148:               whichever pushed last.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Find your results</td><td>Folders <em>and</em> files carry the Linear ticket and the slot,
2149:               with no exception —
2150:               <code class="cm">results-ks-666-slot&lt;n&gt;.json</code>,
2151:               <code class="cm">output/reports-slot&lt;n&gt;/pr-ks-666-&lt;ts&gt;</code>,
2152:               <code class="cm">test-fast-ks-666-&lt;ts&gt;-slot&lt;n&gt;</code>,
2153:               <code class="cm">playwright/results/playwright-report-ks-682-&lt;ts&gt;-slot&lt;n&gt;</code>
2154:               behind a stable
2155:               <code class="cm">results/latest-slot&lt;n&gt;</code> pointer, with

2281:               first; feed failing endpoints into Akto.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Schemathesis + k6</td><td>Functional coverage validation (SC) then load/stress at scale
2282:               (k6). </td></tr><tr><td>Prove correctness before k6 hammers it.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Semgrep + Trivy</td><td>SAST (source) + container/IaC scanning. </td></tr><tr><td>Semgrep finds code flaws;
2283:               Trivy finds dependency &amp; infra vulns.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2">Gitleaks + Semgrep</td><td>Pre-commit (gitleaks) → CI SAST (semgrep). </td></tr><tr><td>Prevent secrets before
2284:               review; deep dataflow analysis in CI.</td></tr></table>

2290: <table class="pmatrix rmatrix"><tr><th>Pitfall</th><th>Fix</th></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">Using Schemathesis as a load tool.</td><td>It sends sequential requests, not concurrent VUs. Use k6 for
2291:                 throughput &amp; latency.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">Relying on Akto for schema validation.</td><td>Akto has no OpenAPI contract awareness. Schemathesis owns
2292:                 conformance.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">k6 v2: keeping removed flags.</td><td>--no-summary → --summary-mode=disabled; k6 cloud script.js → k6
2293:                 cloud run; REST API needs --address.</td></tr><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="1">Running
2294:                 <span style="font-family: monospace">--max-examples</span>
2295:                 uncapped in CI.</td><td>Will time out. Use pr=5 (1.2 min, KS-589 VM 2026-08-11), test-fast=6 (1,860 req
2296:                 by the request model; not re-measured), pre-merge=6 (16.9 min,
2297:                 KS-589 VM 2026-08-11; not re-measured on this Mac) for the local PR/pre-merge runs;

2301:                 <code>run.py nightly</code> (the scheduled workflow is historical).</td></tr></table>

2950: <pre><span class="cm"># Kam ruling 2026-10-02 option (a): widen GET /api/users/lookup to accept a connector token, as POST /api/users/stub already does (KS-564, Option A).</span>
2951: <span class="cm"># WHY: Platform S authenticates with an sk_ connector key, so its token is type:'connector'. /lookup used plain authenticate(), so every S transfer-custody call 401'd and fell back. Both routes now use authenticateAccessOrConnector().</span>
2952: <span class="cm"># THE TOKEN TYPE IS NOT THE PERMISSION — the route's own role/scope gate still runs after it, so `users:read` is the effective gate on /lookup, and a cross-tenant lookup still returns 404 (not 200-empty: positive existence must not be readable from the response shape).</span>
2953: <span class="cm"># AUDIT LABEL is route-neutral on purpose: the log line read "users/stub: ..." unconditionally, so a second accepting route would have written an audit line naming a route it never touched. It now carries route: req.baseUrl + req.path.</span>
2954: <span class="cm">#   MEASURED on GET /api/users/lookup?email=alice%40example.com — req.originalUrl = /api/users/lookup?email=alice%40example.com (leaks the address); req.baseUrl + req.path = /api/users/lookup (does not). originalUrl would defeat maskEmail(); that is why it is not used here.</span>
2955: cd Blockchain/Dev/services/auth
2956: npx vitest run                     <span class="cm"># NOTE: `npm test` in this service is WATCH mode. Use the explicit run form.</span>
2957: npx vitest run <span class="val">src/__tests__/ks1402-lookup-accepts-connector-token.test.ts</span>   <span class="cm"># 183 lines, 4 cells</span>
2958: <span class="flag">CELL 1</span> connector token WITH users:read reaches the handler ....... <span class="val">200</span>
2959: <span class="flag">CELL 2</span> connector token WITHOUT users:read ....................... <span class="val">403</span> <span class="cm"># 403, not 401 — it authenticated, it is not authorised</span>
2960: <span class="flag">CELL 3</span> interactive ACCESS token still works ..................... <span class="val">200</span> <span class="cm"># THE CONTROL: green at base AND at head</span>
2961: <span class="flag">CELL 4</span> tenant-A connector token vs a tenant-B-only email ....... <span class="val">404</span>
2962: <span class="cm"># Cells mint a REAL type:'connector' token via generateConnectorToken. The authenticator is NEVER mocked: 0 mocks of ../middleware/authenticate, against a must-hit control of 9 vi.mock calls elsewhere in the same file. A mocked authenticator cannot observe the thing the ticket is about.</span>
2963: <span class="cm"># RED-FIRST / GREEN-AFTER (2026-10-04): new test + base product code -&gt; cells 1, 2, 4 RED (expected 401 to be 200 / 403 / 404) and cell 3 GREEN. At the PR head -&gt; 4/4 green. Suite 77 -&gt; 78 files, 836 -&gt; 840 tests, both sides on the same base.</span>
2964: <span class="cm"># TIMING — NO ROW TOUCHED, and that is a measurement, not an omission. At the base SHA, in BOTH platform-k docs: `services/auth` 0 hits, `services/transfer` 0, `generate-openapi` 0, `check:openapi` 0 — against a must-hit control of `auth` 52 (flow diagrams) / 59 (this sheet). 3710: <h2>/revoke is one atomic transition — KS-1278</h2>
3711: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="6"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td><code>POST /api/documents/:id/revoke</code> decided
3712:         “already revoked” on a <strong>READ</strong> and then ran an
3713:         <strong>unconditional</strong> <code>UPDATE</code>, so two overlapping revokes could both
3714:         pass the read: <strong>200 + 200</strong>, two updates, two
3715:         <code>action_provenance</code> rows, two anchor calls. </td></tr><tr><td>The decision now lives
3716:         <strong>IN the UPDATE</strong> — <code>updateDocument</code>’s new
3717:         <code>ifStatusIsNot</code> option adds <code>AND (… IS NULL OR status IS DISTINCT
3718:         FROM …)</code> to the <code>WHERE</code>, and a guarded write that changed no row
3719:         returns <code>null</code>. </td></tr><tr><td>The loser answers the <em>same</em> 400 and returns
3720:         <strong>before</strong> <code>recordOnBehalfOf</code>, so it records nothing and anchors
3721:         nothing. <code>Refs KS-1278</code>; the row-lock alternative is not taken.
3722:         <br/><br/><strong>Round 2 (this commit).</strong> The guarded <code>UPDATE</code> still keyed on
3723:         <code>external_id</code>, but both reads fall back to the primary key for a UUID-shaped id
3724:         (<code>documentRepo.ts:244-251</code>) and the API hands clients that key as
3725:         <code>documentUuid</code> (<code>:172</code>). </td></tr><tr><td>So a <strong>sequential, non-race</strong>
3726:         revoke of a live, owned, unrevoked document addressed by its <code>documentUuid</code>
3727:         matched <strong>0 rows</strong> and answered <code>400 “already revoked”</code>
3728:         (gate65 <strong>N-1393-1</strong>). </td></tr><tr><td>The guarded write now keys on <strong>the row the read
3729:         resolved</strong> (<code>:616</code>), mirroring the read’s own precedence. </td></tr><tr><td>Only the
3730:         <strong>one</strong> opted-in caller changes key; the other <strong>12</strong> production
3731:         <code>updateDocument(</code> callers take a byte-identical statement.
3732:       </td></tr></table></div>

3768: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="6"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> The connector allow-list is read from platform settings to

4029: <h2>The transfer reject schema declares signature, so a wrong-typed one is refused — KS-1435</h2>
4030: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="5"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> <code>rejectTransferSchema</code> in
4031:         <code>services/transfer/src/index.ts</code> never declared <code>signature</code>, while the

4033:         does not name, so a wrong-typed <code>signature</code> was <strong>discarded rather than
4034:         refused</strong>: the schema then validated and the reject <em>ran</em> with <strong>200</strong>.
4035:         </td></tr><tr><td>The caller gets a success for a request the contract calls invalid, and the rejection is

4037:         <code>signature: z.string().optional()</code>. The narrowing is the <strong>type</strong>, never the
4038:         presence — <code>optional()</code> is what keeps every existing caller that sends no signature green.

4614: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="4"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> <code>rotate</code> is optional and defaults to <code>false</code>. 4793: <h2>generated_guard_restore keeps the suite's exit status when a cleanup is chained in front &mdash; KS-1738</h2>
4794: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> <code>generated_guard_restore()</code> reads the suite&rsquo;s status as its first statement (<code>local rc=$?</code>). 4831: <h2>The &ldquo;run compared as one value&rdquo; guard and the REAL cell&rsquo;s summary &mdash; KS-1529</h2>
4832: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> The ks1000 file&rsquo;s guard against comparing a checker run as ONE value (status and output inside one array or object) used to be a per-line regex on the array form. It missed an <strong>object</strong>, a <strong>reversed</strong> array and an array <strong>split over several lines</strong>; it is now <code>runsComparedAsOneValue</code>, a scan of the joined text bounded by <code>]</code> or <code>}</code>. A bound of <code>)</code> would miss a nested call ahead of the first field, so a cell plants that shape. </td></tr><tr><td> The REAL cell&rsquo;s expected summary is a named constant, <code>AUTH_GREEN_SUMMARY</code>. A cell proves it can fail (a red run, a silent run with the right status, a wrong-status run), and a second cell reads the REAL cell off the <strong>syntax tree</strong> to prove it still passes the constant. <strong>Both are needed:</strong> with the second cell excluded, the gate&rsquo;s M3 (the REAL cell cut to a bare status check) leaves the whole file green, 83 passed and 0 red. </td></tr></table></div>
4833: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>Gotchas when you run this locally.</strong></td><td> <strong>Plant a shape by assembly, never literally.</strong> The guard scans this file&rsquo;s whole text, strings and comments included, so a literal <code>expect(</code> followed by <code>[</code> or <code>{</code> and both fields flags the file itself. The cells build the plants from <code>'expect' + '('</code>. A permitted shape is the file&rsquo;s own idiom (<code>expect(r.status, r.out)</code> appears in it already), so those cells count occurrences added, not occurrences present. </td></tr><tr><td> <strong>A mutant copy must sit beside the test, and under <code>src/__tests__</code> it is type-checked by the real ratchet.</strong> The cells read <code>__filename</code>, so a copy reads itself; but the REAL cell runs the checker over <code>services/auth</code>, copy included, so a mutant that leaves an unused name reds the REAL cell with TS6133 for that reason and not because of the cell&rsquo;s logic. Delete every copy and check <code>git status</code>. </td></tr><tr><td> <strong>The <code>-t KS-1529</code> filter runs only the new describe.</strong> The rewritten guard cell is in the KS 1519 describe and the REAL cell in the KS 1000 one, so run the whole file to see them. Under load the full suite also times out <code>ks949</code> (5 s test timeout) and <code>auth.integration</code> (10 s HOOK timeout): raise <code>--testTimeout</code> AND <code>--hookTimeout</code>, they are different knobs. </td></tr></table></div>
4834: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>Not measured here.</strong></td><td> A bracket nested ahead of the second field (<code>parts[0]</code>, a nested object literal) is NOT caught &mdash; measured, 0 hits &mdash; and only the REAL cell is protected of the <strong>35</strong> <code>expectRun</code> call sites at base (39 after). The predicate is a substring: <code>10 new; 0 stale baseline entries</code> contains it, though no run with new errors exits 0. </td></tr><tr><td> The four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, Performance) are <strong>UNMEASURED</strong>; nothing on either box. </td></tr></table></div>

4855: <h2>The two arms of leg 14&rsquo;s hook-control refusal are told apart by their Derived line &mdash; KS-1756</h2>
4856: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> <code>preflight.sh:731</code> refuses to run the shell suites when the derived set of the pre-push hook&rsquo;s controls is <strong>empty</strong> or is <strong>non-empty but lacks <code>ALLOW_FORCE</code></strong>. 5055: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="3"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> <code>countUsersInner</code> in <code>Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts</code> now has the catch <code>listUsersInner</code> got in KS 1484. 5196: <h2>AppError subclasses in packages/shared keep their own prototype &mdash; KS-1467</h2>
5197: <div class="note"><table class="pmatrix"><tr><td class="pm-topic" rowspan="2"><strong>What to know.</strong></td><td> Every subclass of <code>AppError</code> in <code>packages/shared</code> (nine, plus <code>DocumentNotFoundError</code> under <code>NotFoundError</code>) used to be reset to the base prototype by the constructor, so <code>err instanceof NotFoundError</code> was always false.
